scope: All 154 current skills and 386 current steps re-reviewed against independently checked sources; 45 historical steps preserved. Numeric criteria are editorial targets, not validated mastery tests.

NAME.title: Name recognition
NAME.previousSharedSetup: Tiny rewards; a familiar quiet room.
NAME.sharedSetupReview: Attention to a name is taught before distraction; a name is not assumed to be a recall or evidence of emotional comfort.

steps.setup: Have tiny rewards within reach in a familiar room. Sit or stand near your relaxed dog, with room for them to move away; no particular posture is needed.
steps.decision: Name-reward pairing precedes the offered head turn; neither requires a sit or eye contact.

steps.setup: Use the same quiet room. Keep rewards out of sight near your body and begin with your dog nearby, comfortably facing a little away from you.
steps.decision: Name-reward pairing precedes the offered head turn; neither requires a sit or eye contact.

MARK.title: Reward marker
MARK.previousSharedSetup: Choose a signal that does not startle your dog.
MARK.sharedSetupReview: Pair the chosen gentle signal with prompt reward; markers are optional and no later action is required after a terminal marker.

steps.setup: Choose a soft spoken word or test the clicker quietly away from your dog first. Put small rewards within easy reach, with your dog comfortably nearby and your reward hand empty.
steps.decision: A marker can be paired directly with reward and must not become a universal training gate.

TOUCH.title: Hand target
TOUCH.previousSharedSetup: Open palm held still beside, not over, the face.
TOUCH.sharedSetupReview: Voluntary empty-hand nose targeting transfers only after the basic contact; do not push a hand into the face.

steps.setup: Sit or stand beside your dog at a comfortable height. Keep one palm empty and rewards in the other hand; leave clear space beside their nose and an open route away.
steps.decision: Voluntary palm contact precedes naming and small placement changes.

steps.setup: Start in the familiar hand-target area on a non-slip floor. Keep your target palm empty, rewards hidden in the other hand, and space for one easy step either side.
steps.decision: Voluntary palm contact precedes naming and small placement changes.

SIT.title: Sit
SIT.previousSharedSetup: Non-slip surface; choose stand instead if sitting seems uncomfortable.
SIT.sharedSetupReview: Comfortable voluntary sitting and early lure fading are appropriate; sitting is not mandatory for safety or proof of calm.

steps.setup: Choose a non-slip area with enough room behind your dog. Have small rewards ready at nose height. If sitting looks uncomfortable, choose a comfortable standing exercise instead.
steps.decision: Comfortable sit acquisition precedes fading food and adding the cue; down and stand are independent.

steps.setup: Use the same non-slip area. Keep the guiding hand empty and rewards in your other hand or pouch, with your dog close enough to see the familiar signal.
steps.decision: Comfortable sit acquisition precedes fading food and adding the cue; down and stand are independent.

DOWN.title: Lie down
DOWN.previousSharedSetup: Soft non-slip surface; no physical pushing.
DOWN.sharedSetupReview: Reward comfortable voluntary lowering without restraint; posture is distinct from relaxation.

steps.setup: Provide a soft, non-slip resting surface and space to stretch out. Sit beside your dog with rewards accessible near floor level; use a comfortable stand or sit as the starting position.
steps.decision: Unforced down acquisition precedes cue transfer; a completed sit is unnecessary.

steps.setup: Use the familiar soft surface and leave space for your dog to stand up between turns. Keep the signaling hand empty and rewards in the other hand or pouch.
steps.decision: Unforced down acquisition precedes cue transfer; a completed sit is unnecessary.

STAND.title: Stand
STAND.previousSharedSetup: Non-slip floor; reward at standing nose height.
STAND.sharedSetupReview: A comfortable stationary stand is useful independently of a down; avoid repeatedly luring the dog to walk forward.

steps.setup: Use a level, non-slip floor with room in front of your dog. Begin beside a freely offered comfortable sit, with a small reward ready at their natural standing nose height.
steps.decision: The dog may already offer a comfortable sit or rise naturally; a recorded sit grade is unnecessary.

FREE.title: Release from a position
FREE.previousSharedSetup: Start with a very easy one-second position. Use any comfortable sit, stand or down your dog already offers; a finished sit lesson is not required.
FREE.sharedSetupReview: A release can be taught from any comfortable position; a completed sit is an unnecessary prerequisite.

steps.setup: Choose a familiar room with non-slip footing and a clear patch of floor for a small tossed reward. Have several rewards ready; any comfortable position your dog already offers is suitable.
steps.decision: Release can be paired from any offered comfortable position, then separated from in-position rewards.

steps.setup: Use the same safe floor area. Have rewards accessible both for delivery at your dog's position and for a small toss away, with an unobstructed route to move off.
steps.decision: Release can be paired from any offered comfortable position, then separated from in-position rewards.

DROP.title: Drop an item
DROP.previousSharedSetup: A low-value dog-safe toy; no guarding history with this setup.
DROP.sharedSetupReview: Trade willingly without chasing or prying; prevention and guarding assessment are distinct from a generic exchange exercise.

steps.setup: Choose an ordinary dog-safe toy your dog does not guard, with floor space to one side for treats. Have better food rewards ready and keep other dogs away. Skip this setup if item handling causes tension.
steps.decision: Easy voluntary trades precede cue-before-reward release, with no retrieve requirement.

steps.setup: Use the same low-value toy and clear trading area, with the better rewards initially out of sight. Avoid treasured or stolen items; a dog with guarding concerns needs an individual plan.
steps.decision: Easy voluntary trades precede cue-before-reward release, with no retrieve requirement.

LEAVE.title: Leave an item alone
LEAVE.previousSharedSetup: Harmless low-interest practice items secured out of reach, better rewards and room to move away. For guarding, use individual professional help rather than approach-and-remove exercises.
LEAVE.sharedSetupReview: Retain the cue, separately reinforce offered disengagement, teach modest context transfer, and keep hazards inaccessible without supervision.

steps.setup: Secure a boring, harmless item behind a barrier or sturdy transparent cover that cannot be knocked aside. Begin far enough away for easy disengagement, with better rewards beside you and away from the item.
steps.decision: Keep the first offered disengagement easy; prevent frustration and avoid implying that staring must continue until a cue.

steps.setup: Prepare one harmless practice item under a sturdy clear cover or behind a secure barrier. Keep the floor clear, better rewards with you and enough distance for an easy turn; protection stays in place.
steps.decision: A cue can be useful without claiming unsupervised protection. The old title contradicted the protected setup.

steps.setup: Prepare a familiar protected harmless item and one similarly boring alternative. Keep both inaccessible and present only one at a time; set rewards away from the item and leave room to retreat.
steps.decision: New context transfer needs its own record; it is not implied by learning the spoken cue.

steps.setup: Use the familiar secured harmless item in a clear room with better rewards ready. Choose a tiny increase in your distance that still permits active supervision; nobody leaves the room.
steps.decision: Handler-distance transfer is new learning. No absent-handler or household-wide safety claim is made.

WAIT.title: Short wait at an indoor doorway
WAIT.previousSharedSetup: An interior door, open floor space, and no escape to outdoors.
WAIT.sharedSetupReview: A short safe interior-door pause can be offered or cued; release and physical exit security remain explicit.

steps.setup: Choose an open interior doorway with no access to outdoors. Clear the floor on both sides, keep the door still, and stand beside your dog with rewards within reach.
steps.decision: Offered doorway pauses are compatible with a release cue; reinforcement can include access through a safe interior doorway.

steps.setup: Use the familiar interior doorway, clear of paws and tails throughout the door's swing. Stand with your dog safely back from the edge and keep rewards available; no exterior exit should be exposed.
steps.decision: Door movement, waiting time and context are separate difficulty dimensions.

TOILET.title: Toilet routine
TOILET.previousSharedSetup: Regular access; investigate new accidents medically.
TOILET.sharedSetupReview: Supervision, frequent individual opportunities and rewarding location are appropriate; medical changes are not disobedience.

steps.setup: Choose an accessible toilet spot and clear the route there. Keep outdoor clothing, a lead if needed, and rewards near the exit so trips after sleep, meals or play can be prompt.
steps.decision: Access routines precede cue pairing. Toilet access must never depend on obedience.

steps.setup: Keep the familiar toilet route immediately accessible and rewards ready at the toilet spot. Choose the same cue in advance; any request signal must leave access to the door unobstructed.
steps.decision: Access routines precede cue pairing. Toilet access must never depend on obedience.

RECALL.title: Come when called, first at home
RECALL.previousSharedSetup: Secure room; hidden rewards; never punish arrival.
RECALL.sharedSetupReview: Teach a distinct inviting approach directly, then transfer gradually; do not assume reliability around hazards or punish arrival.

steps.setup: Use a secure room with a clear, non-slip path between you and your dog. Have attractive rewards out of sight and room to take one step backward without bumping anything.
steps.decision: A distinct recall cue can be paired directly with approach; responding to the dog’s name is independent.

steps.setup: Keep the same enclosed space and clear a slightly longer approach. Have several small rewards accessible at your side. Only include harness contact if your dog already welcomes that separate handling exercise.
steps.decision: Recall words directly predict approach; a name response is helpful but not required.

OTARGET.title: Nose target an object
OTARGET.previousSharedSetup: A large smooth target pad on a stable handle; no sharp ends or detachable small parts.
OTARGET.sharedSetupReview: Teach broad stationary nose contact before placement or motion; this is a reusable contact action, not emotional treatment.

steps.setup: Prepare a large, smooth target pad on a secure handle without sharp ends or loose parts. Sit or stand beside your dog, with rewards in the other hand and room beside their face.
steps.decision: Direct nose contact is acquired before the object-target cue and placement changes.

steps.setup: Use the familiar target and non-slip footing. Leave a few inches of clear space around its usual position at natural head height, and keep rewards separate from the target hand.
steps.decision: Direct nose contact is acquired before the object-target cue and placement changes.

STAY.title: Stay until released
STAY.previousSharedSetup: A quiet enclosed room, non-slip floor and any comfortable position. Duration and distance grow separately.
STAY.sharedSetupReview: Increase short duration, distance and distraction separately; release and comfort matter more than a posture quota.

steps.setup: Choose a quiet enclosed room and comfortable non-slip surface. Have rewards ready for delivery at your dog's position and enough clear floor for an easy release; use any comfortable posture.
steps.decision: The release is an actual end signal; short duration precedes movement and small independent changes.

steps.setup: Use the same surface with clear space behind your own feet for one small step. Keep rewards with you and the dog free to leave; remove nearby distractions before adding handler movement.
steps.decision: The release is an actual end signal; short duration precedes movement and small independent changes.

steps.setup: Prepare a quiet enclosed area with clear footing for a slight turn or two steps away. Decide beforehand whether this turn changes time or movement, and keep rewards readily accessible.
steps.decision: The release is an actual end signal; short duration precedes movement and small independent changes.

STOP.title: Stop and stand on cue
STOP.previousSharedSetup: An enclosed level space; no moving traffic. This cue never replaces a lead or secure boundary.
STOP.sharedSetupReview: Reward a modest stationary pause in protected settings; this does not authorize traffic or off-leash safety tests.

steps.setup: Use a secure, level, non-slip space away from traffic and wildlife. Begin beside your dog with room for a few slow steps and rewards at natural standing nose height.
steps.decision: A familiar stand supports stopping slow movement, then reduced handler prompting and a tiny distance change.

steps.setup: Use the same enclosed area with one or two clear steps between you and your dog. Keep rewards accessible so you can walk to their stopping place without calling them closer.
steps.decision: A familiar stand supports stopping slow movement, then reduced handler prompting and a tiny distance change.

steps.setup: Choose a secure area with an unobstructed, level walking surface. Start only a few steps from your dog, with rewards ready; this exercise needs slow strolling, not running or real hazards.
steps.decision: A familiar stand supports stopping slow movement, then reduced handler prompting and a tiny distance change.

FRONT.title: Come to a front position
FRONT.previousSharedSetup: Non-slip enclosed space. A stand is as valid as a sit; no tight positioning or collisions.
FRONT.sharedSetupReview: A comfortable arrival position is optional and distinct from a safety recall; do not crowd or physically align the dog.

steps.setup: Stand on non-slip flooring with an open approach in front of you. Leave about a comfortable dog's length of space before your knees and have small rewards available at their natural head height.
steps.decision: A broad comfortable approach directly teaches the front position; no completed recall or sit is necessary.

steps.setup: Use the familiar approach area, with your signal hand empty and rewards elsewhere. Clear space at the usual starting spot and one nearby alternative; a comfortable stand is sufficient.
steps.decision: A broad comfortable approach directly teaches the front position; no completed recall or sit is necessary.

FOODWAIT.title: Wait for a food-bowl invitation
FOODWAIT.previousSharedSetup: Use part of the normal meal and a quiet feeding area with one dog. Skip if food handling causes guarding or frustration; meals are never withheld for performance.
FOODWAIT.sharedSetupReview: Keep bowl placement very brief and optional; never make meals conditional, repeatedly remove bowls, or treat guarding through compliance.

steps.setup: Use the usual quiet feeding area with other animals separated. Put part of the normal meal in an easy-to-handle bowl and clear its landing spot. Skip waiting practice if bowl handling causes tension.
steps.decision: Bowl manners are optional; essential nutrition and guarding treatment must not depend on compliance.

steps.setup: Prepare the familiar bowl and clear feeding spot, with a separate small reward accessible. Stand at a comfortable lowering height with your dog free nearby; the meal remains available without a performance requirement.
steps.decision: A momentary pause is paired directly with bowl access; meals and urgent access never depend on a grade.

MAT.title: Go to a mat
MAT.previousSharedSetup: Comfortable non-slip mat, away from triggers.
MAT.sharedSetupReview: Teach voluntary stationing and release separately from relaxed rest; a mat is not an enforced place to endure fear.

steps.setup: Lay a comfortable, flat mat on a non-slip surface away from household traffic. Leave open floor around it for approaches and resets, with small rewards available beside you.
steps.decision: Approach and full-foot arrival precede adding the mat cue; settling and staying are separate behaviors.

steps.setup: Place the familiar mat in its usual quiet spot, with clear floor one step away. Keep rewards with you rather than scattered on the mat before the cue.
steps.decision: Approach and full-foot arrival precede adding the mat cue; settling and staying are separate behaviors.

SETTLE.title: Relax voluntarily on the mat
SETTLE.previousSharedSetup: Work after ordinary needs are met; dog can leave.
SETTLE.sharedSetupReview: Capture comfortable rest independently of cued stationing; a down, food-taking or immobility alone does not establish relaxation.

steps.setup: After ordinary toilet, movement and water needs are met, place a comfortable mat near your quiet activity. Keep low-excitement rewards within reach and an open route off the mat.
steps.decision: Voluntary rest on a comfortable mat can be captured without a trained go-to-mat cue.

steps.setup: Use the familiar resting spot when your dog is already comfortable there. Minimize nearby activity, have quiet rewards ready, and leave their preferred way to get up unobstructed.
steps.decision: Voluntary rest is captured directly; go-to-mat is an optional aid rather than a gate.

steps.setup: Choose a familiar calm resting period and sit near the usual mat or bed. Keep the room uneventful and allow your dog to choose their posture and leave freely.
steps.decision: Voluntary rest is captured directly; go-to-mat is an optional aid rather than a gate.

SAFE.title: Choose a safe resting area
SAFE.previousSharedSetup: Quiet room or open crate only if already comfortable; water and a bed.
SAFE.sharedSetupReview: A refuge requires actual comfort, escape management and trusted support; confinement or isolation is not automatically soothing.

steps.setup: Arrange a quiet bed and water away from the entry and busy windows. Leave the route in and out open; use an open crate only if that space is already comfortable.
steps.decision: Refuge exploration precedes attended management rehearsals. There is no requirement to be left alone.

steps.setup: Prepare the familiar resting area without visitors present. Have a trusted person comfortably visible and a gate, door or curtains ready for only the small adjustment your dog already tolerates.
steps.decision: Refuge exploration precedes attended management rehearsals. There is no requirement to be left alone.

ALONE.title: Very brief comfortable alone time
ALONE.previousSharedSetup: Camera; a familiar safe area; skip to individual help if absences already cause panic.
ALONE.sharedSetupReview: Camera-guided below-distress movement, tiny absences and departure-action comfort are distinct components; no crying-out or duration guarantee.

steps.setup: Place a camera where you can see your dog's whole body in their familiar safe area. Start while they are comfortably resting or occupied, with the floor around your chair clear. Do not test known separation panic.
steps.decision: Comfortable tiny within-room movements precede tiny absences and departure-action combinations.

steps.setup: Check that the camera shows your dog while you are briefly beyond a nearby interior doorway. Keep the return route clear, the door open and the starting distance within their established comfort.
steps.decision: Comfortable tiny within-room movements precede tiny absences and departure-action combinations.

steps.setup: Keep your dog in their comfortable familiar area with a camera available to observe their whole body. Choose one quiet departure action and suitable rewards; this exercise includes no departure.
steps.decision: Departure actions can be conditioned independently; they must not be gated behind out-of-view absences or treated as proof of absence tolerance.

RESTHEAD.title: Rest the head on a cushion
RESTHEAD.previousSharedSetup: A low stable soft cushion; no lifting or positioning the head. Chin placement is not proof of relaxation.
RESTHEAD.sharedSetupReview: Voluntary cushion contact can be taught directly; do not press the head down or infer calm solely from the trained posture.

steps.setup: Place a stable soft cushion at your dog's natural chin height on a non-slip base. Sit beside it with rewards accessible and a clear route away; avoid anything that tips under light contact.
steps.decision: This step teaches cushion contact directly; a hand chin rest is only an optional prompt.

steps.setup: Keep the familiar cushion at the same comfortable height. Sit nearby with quiet rewards and clear space for your dog to lift their head and leave without obstruction.
steps.decision: Cushion contact is shaped directly; a hand chin rest is an optional prompt rather than a prerequisite.

CRATE.title: Rest comfortably in a closed crate
CRATE.previousSharedSetup: A roomy stable crate with a secured door and familiar bedding. Stay present. Skip confinement practice and seek individual help for panic; this does not establish alone-time tolerance.
CRATE.sharedSetupReview: Introduce an optional crate with voluntary entry and gradual comfortable closure; it is unsuitable as compulsory panic management.

steps.setup: Check that the crate allows comfortable standing, turning and lying. Secure the door fully open, add familiar non-slip bedding, and clear the entrance and exit. Remain nearby with rewards.
steps.decision: Voluntary entry precedes door motion, then tiny attended closure. Open refuge, absences and travel remain distinct.

steps.setup: Prepare the familiar roomy crate with the door initially secured open. Keep its swing clear of paws and tails, place rewards within reach, and sit beside rather than across the exit.
steps.decision: Voluntary entry precedes door motion, then tiny attended closure. Open refuge, absences and travel remain distinct.

steps.setup: Check the familiar crate's latch opens smoothly and rewards can be delivered safely without trapping fingers. Stay beside the door with its exit clear; do not use this setup for panic or unattended absences.
steps.decision: Voluntary entry precedes door motion, then tiny attended closure. Open refuge, absences and travel remain distinct.

VACATE.title: Get off furniture on cue
VACATE.previousSharedSetup: A low stable surface, non-slip landing and an unobstructed route. Use a ramp if needed. Skip for pain, sleep disturbance or resource guarding.
VACATE.sharedSetupReview: Reward moving to an inviting alternative without crowding, intimidation or grabbing; existing guarding requires an individual plan.

steps.setup: Use a low, stable surface only while your dog is awake and comfortable. Clear a non-slip landing or familiar ramp, with rewards accessible from the side; skip practice if approaches cause guarding or pain.
steps.decision: A voluntary route to a safe low landing precedes cue transfer; no pressure or high jump.

steps.setup: Keep the same secure landing or ramp and a comfortable alternative resting place nearby. Have the signaling hand empty and rewards ready on the floor side, with your dog awake and unpressured.
steps.decision: A voluntary route to a safe low landing precedes cue transfer; no pressure or high jump.

ALLDONE.title: Finish an activity and move on
ALLDONE.previousSharedSetup: Brief enjoyable play, a safe place to put props and a ready alternative such as water, a sniff or rest. Meet ordinary needs first.
ALLDONE.sharedSetupReview: Pair a predictable end signal with a comfortable transition; it is not punishment or enforced loss of needed interaction.

steps.setup: Choose a brief familiar game, a safe place to put its prop, and a ready alternative such as water, a sniff area or a bed. Arrange a voluntary trade separately if the dog may hold the prop.
steps.decision: A predictable pleasant transition acquires the end cue directly before transfer to another activity.

steps.setup: Select a different easy activity and prepare the same familiar quiet alternative. Clear the route between them and a safe place for equipment, with ordinary movement, water and rest needs already met.
steps.decision: A predictable pleasant transition acquires the end cue directly before transfer to another activity.

CHECK.title: Voluntary check-in
CHECK.previousSharedSetup: Familiar secure space; rewards at your side.
CHECK.sharedSetupReview: Reinforce offered check-ins and gradual transfer; do not demand prolonged eye contact or make food pairing contingent on it.

steps.setup: Choose a familiar enclosed space with something safe to sniff and room beside your body for rewards. Stand comfortably without blocking your dog, with food readily accessible and no attention cue needed.
steps.decision: Offered orientation is rewarded directly before incorporating ordinary walking.

steps.setup: Prepare a clear, quiet walking strip with safe sniffing space nearby. Use comfortable familiar walking equipment if needed, keep the lead slack, and have rewards accessible at your side.
steps.decision: Offered orientation is rewarded directly before incorporating ordinary walking.

LOOSE.title: Loose-leash walking
LOOSE.previousSharedSetup: Secure comfortable walking equipment and an ordinary leash; a quiet practice route. Check fit and willingness directly before practice. If equipment itself causes avoidance, use the Comfortable harness routine separately first.
LOOSE.sharedSetupReview: Teach slack-lead walking on comfortable equipment in small increments; equipment fit is a safety check rather than an obedience grade.

steps.setup: Check that the familiar harness or collar fits comfortably and your dog willingly wears it. Use an ordinary lead in a quiet spacious area, with rewards accessible beside your chosen leg.
steps.decision: Comfortable secure equipment is checked directly; recording a harness lesson is not a necessary learned component.

steps.setup: Choose a short, clear stretch on the familiar quiet route. Check comfortable equipment and slack lead handling, with rewards easy to reach before taking the first walking steps.
steps.decision: Slack-leash movement is taught directly; secure comfortable equipment is checked in the setup, without requiring a harness grade.

steps.setup: Choose a safe, modestly interesting sniffing patch beside a quiet route. Check the ground and other animals, use comfortable equipment, and leave room to approach without tightening the lead.
steps.decision: Slack-leash movement is taught directly; secure comfortable equipment is checked in the setup, without requiring a harness grade.

TURN.title: Happy turn-away
TURN.previousSharedSetup: Teach first with no trigger; enough space for a wide turn.
TURN.sharedSetupReview: Rehearse an inviting turn before mild distraction, without leash corrections; a retreat remains valid regardless of cue response.

steps.setup: Clear a wide turning arc in a quiet room or secure yard with no trigger present. Stand near your dog with rewards ready and stable footing for two easy steps away.
steps.decision: A trigger-free turn cue precedes travel and easy sniff interruptions; equipment comfort is a setup condition.

steps.setup: Pick a quiet outdoor rehearsal area and a safe destination a few steps away. Use familiar comfortable walking equipment and hold the slack lead clear of both your feet.
steps.decision: The learned turn is necessary; suitable comfortable equipment is a direct setup check rather than a mandatory harness grade.

steps.setup: Choose a familiar quiet route and an easy sniffing spot well away from dogs or other triggers. Identify a clear, rewarding exit direction before starting.
steps.decision: A trigger-free turn cue precedes travel and easy sniff interruptions; equipment comfort is a setup condition.

FIND.title: Find food on the ground
FIND.previousSharedSetup: Clean surface; one dog only; no traffic or food competition.
FIND.sharedSetupReview: Invited food search on known safe ground is compatible with leave-it training; avoid competition, ingestion hazards or overwhelming triggers.

steps.setup: Inspect a small clean floor patch and separate other animals. Have a few tiny suitable treats ready, with your dog comfortably nearby and no traffic or food competition.
steps.decision: A visible food scatter acquires its own cue before the ground surface changes.

steps.setup: Check a quiet yard or familiar outdoor patch for litter, unsafe plants and approaching animals. Keep other dogs away and prepare easily visible food pieces off the walking path.
steps.decision: A visible food scatter acquires its own cue before the ground surface changes.

SIDE.title: Move behind you or to the far side
SIDE.previousSharedSetup: A quiet room; an already comfortable hand target.
SIDE.sharedSetupReview: Reward a comfortable side position without physical placement; this optional alignment does not replace free movement and sniffing.

steps.setup: Stand in a quiet room with enough non-slip floor for a wide arc around your legs. Keep the target hand empty, rewards separate, and any lead clear of the route.
steps.decision: The hand target actually guides the broad route; the far-side cue follows this action.

steps.setup: Prepare the same wide side-change space, with room for one forward step after arrival. Keep rewards accessible and avoid real approaching activity during this cue practice.
steps.decision: The hand target actually guides the broad route; the far-side cue follows this action.

HEEL.title: Heel on cue
HEEL.previousSharedSetup: Choose left or right once. Start in an enclosed non-slip room without a leash if safe. Shoulder roughly beside your leg, natural head carriage, no sustained eye contact or tight competition posture.
HEEL.sharedSetupReview: Short precise positioning is optional, with early lure fading and releases; it is not the standard for an entire ordinary walk.

steps.setup: Choose your left or right side in advance. Stand in an enclosed non-slip room with a broad approach arc beside that leg, and have rewards ready at natural nose height.
steps.decision: Entry position is independently trainable; brief movement precedes turns and a learned release at the step that uses its discrimination.

steps.setup: Use the same side and clear entry area. Keep the guiding hand empty and rewards in the other hand, with starting space just ahead and slightly to the side.
steps.decision: Entry position is independently trainable; brief movement precedes turns and a learned release at the step that uses its discrimination.

steps.setup: Clear a short, straight walking strip in the familiar enclosed room. Use your established side and rewards accessible beside that leg; leave enough space for a relaxed release.
steps.decision: Entry position is independently trainable; brief movement precedes turns and a learned release at the step that uses its discrimination.

steps.setup: Prepare a broad turning area with non-slip footing and space for ordinary walking afterward. For outdoor transfer, choose a quiet secure spot and check familiar comfortable equipment before starting.
steps.decision: Entry position is independently trainable; brief movement precedes turns and a learned release at the step that uses its discrimination.

RHYTHM.title: Counted walking rhythm
RHYTHM.previousSharedSetup: A quiet safe space, suitable small rewards and room to opt out. Inspired by Leslie McDevitt’s counting pattern games; this is a predictable activity, not a cure for fear.
RHYTHM.sharedSetupReview: Predictable short walking patterns can help communication; no claim that a pattern cures fear or overrides the need for distance.

steps.setup: Stand in a quiet safe area with your dog freely nearby. Prepare suitable small rewards for delivery beside you, keeping your hands neutral and an open route for the dog to opt out.
steps.decision: Predictable stationary count-reward pairings precede a few optional walking cycles; exact heel position and trigger exposure are not part of this game.

steps.setup: Choose a short, flat walking strip in the familiar quiet area. Have rewards easy to reach beside you, comfortable equipment if needed, and space for a break away from distractions.
steps.decision: Predictable stationary count-reward pairings precede a few optional walking cycles; exact heel position and trigger exposure are not part of this game.

CURB.title: Pause at a curb
CURB.previousSharedSetup: Start with a flat line on a floor, then a quiet path well away from traffic. Humans always decide when a crossing is safe.
CURB.sharedSetupReview: Start at harmless flat lines, then a protected real curb with human traffic decisions; no automatic road-safety claim.

steps.setup: Lay a flat contrasting strip on a non-slip floor, with several clear steps on each side. Avoid raised edges or obstacles and have rewards ready beside your dog.
steps.decision: A harmless floor line teaches the pause before quiet real-edge transfer; no claim that dogs judge traffic.

steps.setup: Choose a protected curb with generous standing space well away from moving vehicles. Check secure comfortable equipment and a clear retreat; an adult remains responsible for every crossing decision.
steps.decision: A harmless floor line teaches the pause before quiet real-edge transfer; no claim that dogs judge traffic.

CROSS.title: Cross a quiet road together
CROSS.previousSharedSetup: A quiet lawful crossing with clear sight lines, comfortable fitted equipment and a capable adult. Rehearse away from vehicles first.
CROSS.sharedSetupReview: Indoor rehearsal follows flat-line preparation; the actual curb prerequisite moves to the real crossing, where humans decide safety.

steps.setup: Mark two harmless flat lines a few steps apart on a non-slip indoor floor. Clear the route between them, prepare rewards beyond the far line, and use a comfortable familiar lead setup.
steps.decision: Indoor route rehearsal needs the flat-line pause, not completed exposure at a real curb.

steps.setup: Choose a quiet lawful crossing with clear sight lines and safe standing space beyond both curbs. A capable adult checks secure equipment and traffic; have rewards accessible for the far side.
steps.decision: Real crossing adds the actual curb context only when that context is introduced.

SLOW.title: Match a slower walking pace
SLOW.previousSharedSetup: A short flat quiet route, suitable equipment and ordinary comfortable walking. This is pace matching, not restricting normal exercise.
SLOW.sharedSetupReview: Reward modest changes to walking pace without force; exercise and pace must suit individual health and normal movement.

steps.setup: Choose a short, flat, unobstructed part of a familiar quiet route. Check comfortable walking equipment and have rewards at your side; begin at your dog's ordinary comfortable pace.
steps.decision: Known slack-leash steps support a small pace change, then a few slower steps.

steps.setup: Use the successful flat route with clear space for alternating normal and slightly slower stretches. Keep rewards accessible; prepare a second equally quiet route only after the familiar one is easy.
steps.decision: Known slack-leash steps support a small pace change, then a few slower steps.

WALKPAUSE.title: Pause while the handler stops
WALKPAUSE.previousSharedSetup: A quiet protected walking space and comfortable secure equipment; no tethering or prolonged immobility.
WALKPAUSE.sharedSetupReview: Practice brief comfortable pauses and release rather than prolonged suppression of exploration or distress.

steps.setup: Choose a protected quiet walking strip and a roomy stopping spot. Check familiar equipment, ordinary toilet and movement needs, and rewards accessible without shortening the lead.
steps.decision: A direct short pause beside a stopped human precedes a brief ordinary hand movement; formal heel is unnecessary.

steps.setup: Use the familiar spacious stopping spot. Have rewards ready and choose one harmless distraction such as an empty pocket or imaginary sign; no tether or busy waiting area is needed.
steps.decision: A direct short pause beside a stopped human precedes a brief ordinary hand movement; formal heel is unnecessary.

DOG.title: Seeing a dog predicts good things
DOG.previousSharedSetup: Open space, clear exit, secure comfortable equipment; cooperative helper and calm adult dog if arranging practice.
DOG.sharedSetupReview: Brief supported sightings and prompt trigger-food pairing begin at a comfortable distance; no obedience or threshold testing is required.

steps.setup: Agree with a capable helper on a calm adult dog, wide separation and a way to end the view. Check comfortable secure equipment and a retreat that does not pass the helper; start conservatively far away.
steps.decision: Assessment should not withhold support until a later lesson.

steps.setup: Use the recorded comfortable separation with the same helper and dog. Arrange brief views that the helper can end, keep desired food ready with you, and leave the retreat completely clear.
steps.decision: An individually comfortable sighting precedes positive pairings, then small controlled movement changes.

steps.setup: Keep the successful distance, secure equipment and retreat unchanged. Agree that the helper will make only one small sideways movement on request; prepare rewards and an immediate way to end the view.
steps.decision: An individually comfortable sighting precedes positive pairings, then small controlled movement changes.

DISENGAGE.title: Choose to look away from another dog
DISENGAGE.previousSharedSetup: Use the already comfortable DOG setup; do not wait through fixation.
DISENGAGE.sharedSetupReview: Teach an offered attention shift at an easy distance, distinct from counterconditioning; never wait through escalating fixation.

steps.setup: Recreate the successful DOG viewing distance with the same calm helper dog, secure equipment and clear retreat. Keep rewards with you and the helper ready to end the view before attention becomes fixed.
steps.decision: Easy sight-food pairing supports comfortable observation before rewarding offered look-aways; no required stare or obedience pose.

steps.setup: Use the established comfortable viewing arrangement and mark out a few clear steps farther away. Coordinate breaks with the helper and keep rewards accessible without tightening the lead.
steps.decision: Easy sight-food pairing supports comfortable observation before rewarding offered look-aways; no required stare or obedience pose.

PARALLEL.title: Walk parallel at a comfortable distance
PARALLEL.previousSharedSetup: Two capable handlers, wide quiet space, no convergence; individualized help for aggression or redirection.
PARALLEL.sharedSetupReview: Both dogs need comfortable wide movement and retreat; trigger-food support need not wait for a check-in or eventual greeting.

steps.setup: Arrange two capable handlers on wide, separate walking lines in a quiet open area. Start at the established comfortable separation, check equipment, and agree on the same direction and outward break routes.
steps.decision: Maintain trigger-food pairing during comfortable movement; check-ins are separately reinforced rather than a condition of support.

steps.setup: Use the same successful separation, direction and calm helper dog. Choose a slightly longer clear stretch with separate sniff-break areas and ample room to widen apart without crossing paths.
steps.decision: Comfort with a moving helper dog and a rehearsed turn support controlled walking and safe exits.

PASS.title: Make a wide planned pass
PASS.previousSharedSetup: An exit route and two handlers; no narrow paths or surprise dogs.
PASS.sharedSetupReview: The first stationary-helper pass needs dog comfort and a turn; moving-helper competence is introduced only for a moving pass.

steps.setup: Place a capable helper and calm stationary dog well away from a broad curved walking line. Check comfortable secure equipment, rewards and a clear exit beyond the arc; avoid narrow paths.
steps.decision: The first pass uses a stationary comfortable helper and a rehearsed exit; completed parallel moving-dog walks and sniff interruptions are unnecessary gates.

steps.setup: Keep the successful wide arc and separate distant helper line. Agree on slow opposite-direction movement and an early-stop signal, with clear exits and rewards available to both handlers.
steps.decision: The moving-helper pass now explicitly needs comfortable dog movement at the step that introduces it.

STRANGER.title: Feel safer with an unfamiliar adult
STRANGER.previousSharedSetup: One cooperative adult, safe distance, open retreat, no children as training helpers.
STRANGER.sharedSetupReview: Use a distant neutral adult with optional retreat, no food lure toward touch and no obligatory greeting.

steps.setup: Arrange a cooperative adult sideways at a generous distance in a quiet open area. Agree that they will ignore your dog without approaching or offering food; keep your own rewards and retreat ready.
steps.decision: Comfortable stationary distant sightings precede tiny adult movements and separate generalization to another person.

steps.setup: Recreate the comfortable adult-helper distance and retreat. Agree on one tiny hand movement and a stop signal, with desired rewards beside you; keep all other helper behavior unchanged.
steps.decision: Comfortable stationary distant sightings precede tiny adult movements and separate generalization to another person.

steps.setup: Arrange a different cooperative adult, beginning again with the stationary sideways posture and original easy distance. Keep secure equipment, your own rewards and an open retreat; no greeting or touch is planned.
steps.decision: Comfortable stationary distant sightings precede tiny adult movements and separate generalization to another person.

KNOCK.title: Feel comfortable hearing a knock
KNOCK.previousSharedSetup: No actual arrivals; prevent surprise knocking while practicing.
KNOCK.sharedSetupReview: Separate a faint controllable tap from mat behavior and the real arrival chain; do not repeat overwhelming knocks waiting for quiet.

steps.setup: Prevent surprise arrivals and choose a quiet time well away from the entrance. Prepare a soft tapping surface and desired rewards; place any helper farther away with a clear stop signal.
steps.decision: A faint harmless tap precedes transfer to the entryway and small changes of count or intensity.

steps.setup: Arrange a helper outside the closed entry door with no visitor entering. Keep your dog at the previously comfortable indoor distance, rewards beside you, and an agreed signal for one very soft tap.
steps.decision: A faint harmless tap precedes transfer to the entryway and small changes of count or intensity.

steps.setup: Keep the successful closed-door arrangement and a helper who can stop immediately. Agree beforehand on either an extra faint tap or a slightly stronger single tap, with rewards and quiet breaks ready.
steps.decision: A faint harmless tap precedes transfer to the entryway and small changes of count or intensity.

BELL.title: Feel comfortable hearing the doorbell
BELL.previousSharedSetup: Controllable recording first; someone can operate the real bell on request.
BELL.sharedSetupReview: Faint recording and physical bell are separate contexts; pair the noticed sound without requiring silence or a station first.

steps.setup: Prepare a brief bell recording and a speaker you can stop immediately. Set a faint volume with the speaker away from your dog's resting area, prevent actual arrivals, and have desired rewards ready.
steps.decision: A faint recording precedes a controllable real bell. An unmodifiable frightening bell needs management, not forced advancement.

steps.setup: Arrange a helper at the actual bell without anyone entering. Keep your dog far inside with rewards ready and the door closed; use a recording instead if the real bell cannot be made sufficiently gentle.
steps.decision: A faint recording precedes a controllable real bell. An unmodifiable frightening bell needs management, not forced advancement.

DOOR.title: Knock means go to the mat
DOOR.previousSharedSetup: Dog is already comfortable with the selected knock; no visitors yet.
DOOR.sharedSetupReview: Combine fluent arrival components under controlled rehearsal; an entry-management plan remains necessary for unplanned arrivals.

steps.setup: Place the familiar mat at an easy distance from the closed entry door. Use only the previously comfortable knock, with rewards ready at the mat and no visitors or unexpected arrivals planned.
steps.decision: The comfortable practical knock, mat arrival and release are actual links in this cue chain; handler door movement follows it.

steps.setup: Keep the successful mat location and gentle knock source unchanged. Have rewards ready for delivery on the mat and enough quiet time for short pauses; no visitor or extra door movement is included.
steps.decision: The comfortable practical knock, mat arrival and release are actual links in this cue chain; handler door movement follows it.

steps.setup: Secure a separate barrier before any entry opening. Place the mat at its successful distance, clear the handler's route to the door, and prepare rewards; nobody will enter during practice.
steps.decision: The comfortable practical knock, mat arrival and release are actual links in this cue chain; handler door movement follows it.

VISITOR.title: Comfortable separated visitor routine
VISITOR.previousSharedSetup: Cooperative adult; trusted company if needed; secure barrier; no bite-risk exposure without professional support.
VISITOR.sharedSetupReview: A fully separated comfortable visit is a valid endpoint; optional distant viewing must not block nonvisual visitor-action practice.

steps.setup: Prepare the dog's already comfortable refuge, a secure barrier and a suitable familiar activity if enjoyed. Arrange trusted company if needed and clear your route to the entry; no visitor is present.
steps.decision: Comfortable refuge management precedes actual arrivals; distant viewing explicitly uses the familiar stranger-comfort work.

steps.setup: Arrange one cooperative adult for a no-knock arrival and a quiet seat away from the refuge. Secure your dog in the familiar comfortable arrangement first, with monitoring or trusted company and rewards ready.
steps.decision: Comfortable refuge management precedes actual arrivals; distant viewing explicitly uses the familiar stranger-comfort work.

steps.setup: Only use an established safe separated arrangement and comfortable STRANGER starting distance. Seat the adult behind a secure barrier, keep your own rewards ready, and ensure you can end the view immediately.
steps.decision: Comfortable refuge management precedes actual arrivals; distant viewing explicitly uses the familiar stranger-comfort work.

steps.setup: Recreate the successful separated or viewing arrangement with the same adult and secure barrier. Agree on one quiet word or small movement and a stop signal, with your rewards and retreat ready.
steps.decision: An optional view must not become a gate for nonvisual visitor practice.

GREET.title: Four paws greeting with familiar people
GREET.previousSharedSetup: Only a comfortable familiar adult; this is not stranger-fear treatment.
GREET.sharedSetupReview: Greeting is voluntary and unnecessary for successful coexistence; approach for food is not permission to touch.

steps.setup: Arrange one familiar adult your dog already enjoys, beginning at an easy distance. Clear a non-slip approach and retreat, have rewards ready low beside you, and agree on one slow approach step.
steps.decision: Four-paw comfort during an easy approach precedes optional voluntary contact; sitting is not required.

steps.setup: Use the familiar adult and successful roomy approach area. Agree that contact is optional and brief, with pauses and an unobstructed exit; keep rewards available without drawing the dog into touch.
steps.decision: Four-paw comfort during an easy approach precedes optional voluntary contact; sitting is not required.

HANDOFF.title: Change leash handlers comfortably
HANDOFF.previousSharedSetup: Two capable familiar adults, a secure enclosed rehearsal area and suitable equipment. Maintain human control of the lead throughout; no stranger handovers.
HANDOFF.sharedSetupReview: Use a familiar consenting helper and reversible small changes; transferred equipment does not justify restraint or separation distress.

steps.setup: Choose a secure enclosed walking area and two familiar capable adults. Check comfortable fitted equipment; the usual handler keeps the lead while the helper has rewards and space to walk nearby.
steps.decision: Comfort with both familiar adults precedes a stationary controlled lead transfer and only then a few steps.

steps.setup: Pause in the enclosed area with the usual handler securely holding the lead. Identify a safe hand-to-hand grip away from your dog's head and remove tangles; have rewards accessible without releasing control.
steps.decision: Comfort with both familiar adults precedes a stationary controlled lead transfer and only then a few steps.

steps.setup: Recreate the successful secure transfer arrangement, with a short clear walking line and the first adult staying close. Check equipment and rewards before the familiar helper takes control; no departure is planned.
steps.decision: Comfort with both familiar adults precedes a stationary controlled lead transfer and only then a few steps.

SOUND.title: Controlled sound practice
SOUND.previousSharedSetup: One chosen sound; controllable speaker; quiet home; stop playback immediately if needed.
SOUND.sharedSetupReview: Controlled brief sound-food pairing changes one dimension at a time; replace historical no-comfort guidance and avoid recording-to-real-event guarantees.

steps.setup: Choose one brief sound clip in a quiet home and a player with an immediate stop control. Set a faint volume and distant speaker position, note both settings, and keep desired food ready.
steps.decision: One comfortable low-intensity pairing precedes one-variable changes and source transfer.

steps.setup: Recreate the successful recording, speaker position and volume. Decide on one tiny duration or volume change before starting, with an immediate stop control and rewards within reach.
steps.decision: One comfortable low-intensity pairing precedes one-variable changes and source transfer.

steps.setup: Choose one modest source or location variation and reset playback to an easy quiet level. Keep the dog's familiar retreat open, rewards ready, and real frightening noise events outside this practice.
steps.decision: One comfortable low-intensity pairing precedes one-variable changes and source transfer.

OUTSIDE.title: Noises outside and window activity
OUTSIDE.previousSharedSetup: Blinds/window film or greater distance; safe retreat into the home.
OUTSIDE.sharedSetupReview: Different mild outdoor sights and sounds need separately controlled starts; visual and auditory presentations are not interchangeable certification.

steps.setup: Prepare a comfortable resting area away from busy windows, with view screening and an open retreat. Check any gentle masking sound separately and have rewards ready while nothing is happening outside.
steps.decision: Management and easy event pairings precede adding the already learned turn away at the action that uses it.

steps.setup: Use the screened comfortable area and agree on one faint scheduled event with a helper far outside. Keep food beside you, a clear stop signal and the option to end exposure immediately.
steps.decision: Management and easy event pairings precede adding the already learned turn away at the action that uses it.

steps.setup: Keep the established low-level event and screening arrangement. Clear a short route away from the window to the familiar rest area, with rewards ready there and no obstacle to retreat.
steps.decision: Management and easy event pairings precede adding the already learned turn away at the action that uses it.

STORM.title: Prepare for unavoidable noise events
STORM.previousSharedSetup: Discuss severe noise fear with your vet before the event; this is a management plan.
STORM.sharedSetupReview: Rehearse protection and support before real events; plan readiness can be recorded without inducing noise or claiming fear is cured.

steps.setup: Choose a quiet day to prepare familiar bedding, curtains and secure exits in the refuge. Have water and trusted company available; use masking sound only if already comfortable and follow any veterinary plan as prescribed.
steps.decision: Support and management must be accessible immediately; this step rehearses the refuge itself without requiring an earlier grade.

steps.setup: On a quiet day, have your refuge checklist, support contacts and any existing veterinary instructions ready. Rehearse ordinary preparations without noise exposure; no storm or fireworks event is needed.
steps.decision: A support plan can be ready before an unavoidable event occurs. Completion must not require manufactured exposure or imply a cure.

OBJECT.title: Comfort with an object or appliance
OBJECT.previousSharedSetup: Object off and stationary first; dog can leave without crossing its path.
OBJECT.sharedSetupReview: Still sight, motion and sound can be conditioned separately; food does not require exploration, and combinations await comfortable components.

steps.setup: Place the object switched off and stable at a generous distance. Keep your dog's route away clear without crossing its path, have rewards with you, and screen part of the view if needed.
steps.decision: Counterconditioning does not require approach, calm exploration or obedience before food.

steps.setup: Keep the object switched off at its established comfortable distance. Arrange a helper for one tiny movement and an immediate stop, with your dog's exit clear and food ready beside you.
steps.decision: Comfortable sight precedes small object movement, then separately introduced appliance sound.

steps.setup: Prepare a faint recording or a helper controlling the appliance behind a distant closed door. Keep the dog in a comfortable separate area with rewards and an immediate sound cutoff; do not add visible motion yet.
steps.decision: Sound conditioning can begin independently of visible movement; combinations require both components to be comfortable.

MOTION.title: Bikes, moving vehicles, or joggers at a distance
MOTION.previousSharedSetup: Safe stationary location away from traffic; no off-leash chase practice.
MOTION.sharedSetupReview: Start well away from traffic or controlled moving helpers with retreat; use physical security and avoid motion-based flooding.

steps.setup: Choose one trigger type and a protected stationary viewing spot with a clear retreat. Arrange a cooperative adult far away for a slow controlled demonstration, check secure equipment, and keep rewards ready.
steps.decision: Comfortable distant slow movement precedes a tiny speed or duration change; no approach or chase.

steps.setup: Keep the successful protected location and wide separation. Agree with the helper on either a very small speed change or a duration change, with a stop signal, secure equipment and rewards available.
steps.decision: Comfortable distant slow movement precedes a tiny speed or duration change; no approach or chase.

CAR.title: Comfort around a parked car
CAR.previousSharedSetup: Parked car in a comfortable temperature; doors secure; vet review for nausea/pain.
CAR.sharedSetupReview: Stationary-car comfort precedes travel; use appropriate transport restraint and veterinary assessment of motion sickness or severe distress.

steps.setup: Park in a safe quiet place, switch the engine off and check a comfortable temperature. Secure doors against unexpected movement, choose an open retreat, and have rewards ready at a comfortable viewing distance.
steps.decision: Comfortable observation precedes voluntary entry, then stationary restraint and door-closure preparation.

steps.setup: Keep the parked engine-off car cool and the door secured open. Prepare stable non-slip footing or a suitable ramp and a clear immediate exit, with rewards accessible both inside and outside.
steps.decision: Comfortable observation precedes voluntary entry, then stationary restraint and door-closure preparation.

steps.setup: Use the familiar travel restraint in the comfortable parked car with a trusted adult beside the dog. Keep doors under human control and the exit clear; engine noise and driving are not part of this setup.
steps.decision: Comfortable observation precedes voluntary entry, then stationary restraint and door-closure preparation.

ELEVATOR.title: Ride a quiet elevator comfortably
ELEVATOR.previousSharedSetup: Use a quiet authorized elevator with a helper, non-slip footing and enough room. Keep dogs and equipment clear of door tracks; humans control access and never use the dog to hold doors.
ELEVATOR.sharedSetupReview: Introduce empty-car sounds, voluntary entry and a short ride separately; keep dog and handler together with no leash through closing doors.

steps.setup: Choose a quiet authorized elevator and a roomy viewing position well outside its doorway. Arrange a helper, secure comfortable equipment, rewards and an unobstructed retreat; avoid passenger traffic.
steps.decision: Door-cycle observation precedes stationary voluntary entry before a tiny attended ride.

steps.setup: Arrange a helper to operate door controls according to building rules. Use an empty stationary car with non-slip footing, enough turning room and lead slack; keep all feet and equipment clear of the door tracks.
steps.decision: Prevent a line crossing a closing elevator door; enter and exit together with ordinary short equipment.

steps.setup: Plan one short quiet ride after comfortable entries. Have a familiar adult beside the dog, rewards ready and a clear exit at the destination; avoid crowds and keep the lead away from door tracks.
steps.decision: Door-cycle observation precedes stationary voluntary entry before a tiny attended ride.

AUTODOOR.title: Pass through automatic doors
AUTODOOR.previousSharedSetup: A quiet permitted entrance with a helper, broad clearance and room to retreat. Humans verify the sensor and opening; avoid revolving doors.
AUTODOOR.sharedSetupReview: Observe safely before a controlled broad passage; never rely on a sensor detecting a dog or put the dog in the opening to activate it.

steps.setup: Choose a quiet permitted entrance with a cooperative helper. Stand to one side outside the sensor area, with secure equipment, rewards and a broad retreat; the helper will activate the panels.
steps.decision: Comfortable panel observation precedes a fully human-checked wide passage; a trained hoop pass is unrelated.

steps.setup: Arrange the helper to activate the doors and verify a fully open, generous passage. Clear the approach and far-side reward area, check lead and tail clearance, and retain room to turn away before entry.
steps.decision: Keep handler and dog together, and ordinary leash clear of automatic doors.

HARNESS.title: Comfortable harness routine
HARNESS.previousSharedSetup: Comfortable fit that allows movement; clip-around style may suit head-shy dogs.
HARNESS.sharedSetupReview: Voluntary approach, head passage and comfortable fitting are separate; fit, movement and withdrawal matter more than a completed grade.

steps.setup: Have the harness unfastened in a quiet room, with rewards separate and room for your dog to move away. Check the buckle sound away from them and begin at a comfortable viewing distance.
steps.decision: Appearance and buckle comfort precede voluntary placement, then fastening and a few steps.

steps.setup: Open the harness fully, keep straps untangled and choose a design that suits your dog, including clip-around if needed. Sit beside them with rewards ready and no obstacle to head withdrawal or leaving.
steps.decision: Appearance and buckle comfort precede voluntary placement, then fastening and a few steps.

steps.setup: Check comfortable fit and smooth clip operation before starting. Use a clear indoor walking area, keep rewards accessible, and remain able to unfasten promptly without trapping legs or skin.
steps.decision: Appearance and buckle comfort precede voluntary placement, then fastening and a few steps.

MUZZLE.title: Comfortable basket muzzle
MUZZLE.previousSharedSetup: Basket with generous pant room; drink/treat access; no unattended wear. Get help for guarding or head-handling fear.
MUZZLE.sharedSetupReview: Use a properly fitted basket allowing full panting and drinking, voluntary entry and gradual straps; no unattended wear or exposure beyond comfort.

steps.setup: Prepare a suitable basket muzzle and small rewards separately. Check sizing with knowledgeable help: allow full panting, drinking and treat access. Begin in a roomy quiet area; seek individual help for guarding or head-handling fear.
steps.decision: Appearance precedes voluntary entry, tiny duration, straps, then comfortable movement; none certifies exposure safety.

steps.setup: Hold the familiar basket at natural nose height with straps secured out of the opening. Keep rewards available through the front and leave space for immediate withdrawal; no fastening is planned. Check full panting room before using the basket.
steps.decision: Appearance precedes voluntary entry, tiny duration, straps, then comfortable movement; none certifies exposure safety.

steps.setup: Use the familiar basket with full pant room and accessible rewards. Keep the buckle and straps loose and reachable for separate quiet practice, with the dog free to withdraw throughout.
steps.decision: Appearance precedes voluntary entry, tiny duration, straps, then comfortable movement; none certifies exposure safety.

steps.setup: Check fitted strap length, quick access to the buckle and full pant/drink room. Prepare rewards through the basket and a quiet supervised area; keep both hands available for prompt safe removal.
steps.decision: Appearance precedes voluntary entry, tiny duration, straps, then comfortable movement; none certifies exposure safety.

steps.setup: Choose a short familiar pleasant activity with water available and continuous supervision. Check secure attachment, full panting space and rubbing before use; for outdoor transfer, choose a quiet route away from triggers.
steps.decision: Appearance precedes voluntary entry, tiny duration, straps, then comfortable movement; none certifies exposure safety.

CHIN.title: Voluntary chin rest
CHIN.previousSharedSetup: Dog comfortable with hands near the face; no painful area handling.
CHIN.sharedSetupReview: A voluntary start and immediate withdrawal are trained communication, not proof of calm or permission to hold the dog through discomfort.

steps.setup: Sit beside your dog with an empty palm or folded towel just below natural chin height. Support any towel securely, keep rewards separate, and leave room to lift the head and move away.
steps.decision: Direct voluntary contact precedes a short freely ended start signal.

steps.setup: Use the familiar chin target at the same comfortable height. Keep your supporting hand still, rewards readily available and the route away clear; do not plan additional handling during this step.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

HANDLE.title: Cooperative gentle handling
HANDLE.previousSharedSetup: Only healthy comfortable areas; veterinary direction for painful or urgent care.
HANDLE.sharedSetupReview: Healthy shoulder movement and momentary touch precede small changes; stop for whole-body discomfort even if the chin remains in position.

steps.setup: Choose a healthy comfortable shoulder area and sit beside your dog with the familiar chin target ready. Keep the other hand initially clear of the body and rewards within reach; urgent or painful care needs veterinary direction.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

steps.setup: Prepare the same healthy shoulder area and freely offered chin target. Keep rewards accessible and your touching hand light and easy to withdraw; no restraint or hidden procedure is part of this turn.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

BRUSH.title: Comfort with a brush or towel
BRUSH.previousSharedSetup: Suitable gentle tool; skin healthy; dog can leave.
BRUSH.sharedSetupReview: Separate tool presence, tiny strokes and small area/duration changes; mats, pain and forced grooming need an individual professional plan.

steps.setup: Choose a soft suitable brush or towel and a quiet non-slip area. Keep the tool at a comfortable initial distance, rewards separate, and an open exit; avoid sore skin and tangled coat.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

steps.setup: Use the familiar soft tool and a healthy tangle-free shoulder area. Sit beside rather than over your dog, with rewards ready and their voluntary start or free approach available; do not hold them in place.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

NAIL.title: Paw-care preparation
NAIL.previousSharedSetup: Non-slip surface; healthy paws; knowledgeable guidance before actual trimming.
NAIL.sharedSetupReview: Paw handling and tool presence can be learned separately; no app completion authorizes clipping anatomy or restraining a paw.

steps.setup: Provide a non-slip surface where your dog can comfortably stand or lie. Choose a healthy upper leg, keep rewards ready and your hands visible; sore or newly sensitive paws need veterinary assessment first.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

steps.setup: Prepare a nail tool for viewing only at a comfortable distance, with any sound controllable separately. Keep paws untouched, rewards ready and the dog free to leave; actual trimming requires individual instruction.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

TEETH.title: Voluntary toothbrushing preparation
TEETH.previousSharedSetup: Veterinary clearance for any dental pain; a demonstrated technique, pet-safe paste and soft suitable brush. No human toothpaste or forced jaw opening.
TEETH.sharedSetupReview: Use veterinary demonstration, pain assessment and pet-safe materials; tiny voluntary lip and outer-tooth work do not replace dental care.

steps.setup: Have a soft pet brush and veterinarian-approved pet toothpaste ready separately from rewards. Use a comfortable non-slip area and obtain veterinary advice for oral pain; no human toothpaste or mouth handling is needed here.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

steps.setup: First obtain a veterinary demonstration of a suitable outer-lip approach. Prepare the familiar chin target, clean hands and rewards beside your dog, with an open exit; do not proceed with pain or guarding concerns.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

steps.setup: Following the veterinary demonstration, prepare the suitable soft pet brush and approved paste if appropriate. Use the familiar voluntary care position with rewards ready; no forced jaw opening or restraint is planned.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

SCALE.title: Comfort on a floor scale
SCALE.previousSharedSetup: A broad stable non-slip low veterinary or pet scale, secured against wobbling; no elevated platform or forced placement.
SCALE.sharedSetupReview: Secure low non-slip surfaces and voluntary steps precede a reading pause; avoid lifting paws or slippery elevated equipment.

steps.setup: Secure a broad low pet scale against wobbling on a non-slip floor. Leave space around it for investigation and retreat, with rewards beside you and no need to lift the dog onto it.
steps.decision: Surface comfort precedes voluntary entry, then a short supported weigh-in pause.

steps.setup: Use the same broad secured scale with clear, level on-and-off routes. Check grip and space for all four feet, keep rewards ready, and allow the dog to go around instead.
steps.decision: Surface comfort precedes voluntary entry, then a short supported weigh-in pause.

steps.setup: Prepare the familiar stable scale and a quiet handler position where its display can be read without crowding the dog. Keep rewards accessible and the step-off route completely clear.
steps.decision: Surface comfort precedes voluntary entry, then a short supported weigh-in pause.

CLIP.title: Accept a leash clip
CLIP.previousSharedSetup: Comfortable already-worn equipment, a quiet light clip and a freely accessible exit. Check fit separately; no reaching to grab the dog.
CLIP.sharedSetupReview: Tiny sound and approach precede clip contact; equipment operation and whole-body comfort remain separate checks.

steps.setup: Start with comfortable already-worn equipment and your dog awake and free to leave. Have a quiet light clip, rewards and room for a visible hand approach; check equipment fit separately.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

steps.setup: Use the familiar attachment point and clip in a quiet clear area. Support the loose lead so it cannot swing into legs, keep rewards accessible, and leave room for an immediate release and a few easy steps. Check comfort and fit before attaching the lead.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

COLLAR.title: Comfortable collar contact
COLLAR.previousSharedSetup: Well-fitted comfortable equipment and an awake willing dog. Touch only; no jerks, choking or surprise grabs. Useful for safe handling but not a test of restraint tolerance.
COLLAR.sharedSetupReview: Reward gentle voluntary collar contact without grabbing or coercion; stop for avoidance rather than relying solely on a start posture.

steps.setup: Choose a quiet moment with your dog awake and willing in familiar well-fitted equipment. Sit or stand to the side with visible hands, rewards ready and an open retreat; skip for guarding or bite risk.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

steps.setup: Use the successful comfortable side position and a safe reachable section of equipment. Keep rewards accessible and the lead slack, with room to release your fingers immediately without pressure on neck or body.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

RINSE.title: Step into a shallow paw rinse
RINSE.previousSharedSetup: A broad stable non-slip tray, shallow lukewarm plain water, dry safe exits and healthy paws. No detergents or forced immersion; veterinary advice for skin problems.
RINSE.sharedSetupReview: Sound, tiny water exposure and comfortable body areas are separate; temperature, footing and freedom to stop remain essential.

steps.setup: Secure a broad empty tray on a non-slip floor, with room for all feet and a dry easy exit. Check healthy paws and smooth edges; keep rewards with you and no water present.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

steps.setup: While your dog is away, dampen only a small part of the familiar secured tray with lukewarm plain water. Prepare a dry non-slip exit and rewards; avoid pouring or splashing near them. Use healthy paws only; follow veterinary advice for skin problems.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

steps.setup: Prepare very shallow lukewarm plain water in the familiar broad non-slip tray. Keep a dry secure exit ready, rewards accessible and supervision continuous; avoid detergents and follow veterinary advice for skin problems.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

EAR.title: Offer an outer-ear check
EAR.previousSharedSetup: Healthy pain-free ears, clean hands and a known chin start signal. No insertion, flushing, cleaning or medication in this lesson; contact a vet for pain, odor or discharge.
EAR.sharedSetupReview: Veterinary guidance and healthy external-ear touch precede limited care; no insertion or treatment decision follows from training alone.

steps.setup: With clean hands, sit beside your dog and prepare the familiar chin target and rewards. Work only around a healthy pain-free ear with room to withdraw; odor, discharge or pain needs a vet instead.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

steps.setup: Use the veterinary team's demonstrated outer-flap approach, clean hands and the familiar chin start target. Keep rewards ready and all instruments away; no insertion, cleaning, flushing or medication is included. Work only with healthy, pain-free ears.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

SIDELIE.title: Lie comfortably on one side
SIDELIE.previousSharedSetup: A broad soft non-slip surface and comfortable movement. Skip for stiffness or breathing difficulty. This posture is not permission for procedures.
SIDELIE.sharedSetupReview: An optional voluntary floor posture uses tiny comfortable changes; it is neither an alpha roll nor permission to immobilize for care.

steps.setup: Provide a broad soft non-slip resting area and sit beside it with quiet rewards. Begin during a voluntarily offered comfortable down, leaving head and limbs free; skip for stiffness or breathing difficulty.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

steps.setup: Keep the familiar soft surface broad enough for a full side rest and easy rising. Sit at natural head level with rewards low and accessible, without placing hands against shoulders or legs.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

steps.setup: Use the same comfortable resting surface and clear exit, with your invitation hand empty and rewards separate. Choose the dog's comfortable side; no handling procedure or increased hold is planned.
steps.decision: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

RAMP.title: Walk a low stable ramp
RAMP.previousSharedSetup: A broad dog-suitable ramp with grip and side clearance, initially flat and later minimally inclined. Secure both ends. Get individual mobility advice for pain or weakness; no vehicle heights in this lesson.
RAMP.sharedSetupReview: Begin flat and stable, then very low with traction; no jumping, elevation prescription or assumed suitability for pain or injury.

steps.setup: Lay a broad dog-suitable ramp flat on level non-slip ground and secure both ends. Clear side space and both exits, with rewards accessible; obtain individual advice for pain or weakness.
steps.decision: A flat secured pass precedes a tiny supported slope; a scale or raised-platform grade is unrelated.

steps.setup: With the dog elsewhere, secure one ramp end on a very low stable support according to its instructions. Check grip and both ends, clear the lower exit, and use a helper only to stabilize equipment. Pain or weakness needs individual mobility advice before practice.
steps.decision: A flat secured pass precedes a tiny supported slope; a scale or raised-platform grade is unrelated.

SCRATCH.title: Scratch a designated board
SCRATCH.previousSharedSetup: A stable broad board with a safe mild surface chosen with your veterinary or grooming team, no staples or loose grit. Healthy paws only. This teaches participation, not a nail-trimming prescription.
SCRATCH.sharedSetupReview: A secured safe scratch surface can be enrichment; nail health and tool suitability need individual assessment, not forced paw placement.

steps.setup: Secure a broad board nearly flat on a non-slip floor. Use a mild safe surface chosen with your veterinary or grooming team, without staples or loose grit; keep rewards above the board and check healthy paws.
steps.decision: Direct foot movement on a stable board precedes naming one tiny scrape; nail contact and clipping are separate.

steps.setup: Prepare the familiar secured board and clear step-off space. Keep rewards separate and hands free to inspect paws afterward; use the agreed mild surface, with only one or two gentle actions planned.
steps.decision: Direct foot movement on a stable board precedes naming one tiny scrape; nail contact and clipping are separate.

BREAKBUTTON.title: Press to request a break
BREAKBUTTON.previousSharedSetup: A large quiet low-force button, different from other request controls, within easy reach and out of chewing access. All ordinary withdrawal remains valid; never require a button press to stop.
BREAKBUTTON.sharedSetupReview: Give a simple trained break signal an actual pause; a button press is not required before respecting avoidance or withdrawal.

steps.setup: Place a separate large quiet low-force break button on a non-slip base within easy reach. Prepare an open route to sniffing or rest and an easy familiar activity; every ordinary withdrawal still ends the turn.
steps.decision: A known button press is immediately honored as a break before offered requests; ordinary withdrawal always remains valid.

steps.setup: Keep the familiar break button safely reachable beside an easy activity, with your hands neutral and the route away open. Plan to stop immediately for any request or ordinary disengagement; no frustration test is needed.
steps.decision: A known button press is immediately honored as a break before offered requests; ordinary withdrawal always remains valid.

TAKE.title: Take a safe object
TAKE.previousSharedSetup: Light dog-safe object too large to swallow; no guarding or painful mouth.
TAKE.sharedSetupReview: Shape voluntary gentle pickup and reward each marker promptly; reset only after willing release or trade, without mouth insertion.

steps.setup: Choose a light dog-safe object too large to swallow, without loose parts or a history of guarding. Sit beside your dog with rewards separate and the object at natural mouth height; skip for mouth pain.
steps.decision: Reinforce one small criterion at a time and reset only after voluntary release or trade; avoid taking objects forcibly.
