steps.setup: Use the familiar safe object at its successful height, with rewards out of sight and an easy trade ready. Leave open floor for any dropped object rather than arranging a carry route yet.
steps.decision: A grip marker earns prompt reward; release to eat is accepted without an additional obedience demand.

HOLD.title: Hold gently
HOLD.previousSharedSetup: Known take and drop; use an ordinary safe toy.
HOLD.sharedSetupReview: Build momentary gentle supported grip before carrying; accept release to eat and never close the jaw or add neck resistance.

steps.setup: Choose the familiar light safe toy and a quiet non-slip area. Sit at a comfortable mouth height with room to support the toy lightly, rewards ready and an easy voluntary release available.
steps.decision: Known take and release support safe brief holds, then unsupported weight and slightly longer duration.

steps.setup: Use the same light object and comfortable presentation position. Keep a receiving palm close beneath it and rewards accessible, with clear floor for a dropped item and no tension against the grip.
steps.decision: Known take and release support safe brief holds, then unsupported weight and slightly longer duration.

GIVE.title: Deliver into your hand
GIVE.previousSharedSetup: Comfortable take/drop; empty receiving palm below the object.
GIVE.sharedSetupReview: A gentle hand delivery uses known object handling, without prying; receiving the item is separately reinforced before travel.

steps.setup: Prepare the familiar light toy, small rewards and an empty receiving palm just below its natural holding height. Sit beside your dog in a quiet area without crowding the mouth.
steps.decision: A short comfortable hold and release are actual components of hand delivery, which is then named separately.

steps.setup: Keep the familiar object and receiving palm nearby at the successful height, with rewards out of sight. Leave enough hand space for a comfortable release without reaching into the mouth.
steps.decision: A short comfortable hold and release are actual components of hand delivery, which is then named separately.

CARRY.title: Carry a few steps
CARRY.previousSharedSetup: Quiet non-slip space; known gentle hold and hand delivery.
CARRY.sharedSetupReview: Add very short transport after a comfortable grip and delivery; mark the completed action rather than ending a carry prematurely.

steps.setup: Clear one slow backward step on non-slip flooring. Prepare the familiar light object, a receiving palm near its holding height and rewards with you; make sure your own retreat is unobstructed.
steps.decision: Comfortable unsupported hold and hand delivery precede a few inches of travel, then a few steps.

steps.setup: Choose a short straight, boring non-slip path of up to three steps. Use the familiar light object and receiving-hand finish, with rewards ready and no other dogs or tempting toys nearby.
steps.decision: Comfortable unsupported hold and hand delivery precede a few inches of travel, then a few steps.

FETCH.title: Retrieve a placed toy
FETCH.previousSharedSetup: Known carry and give; begin with a stationary item rather than a throw.
FETCH.sharedSetupReview: Stationary pickup needs hand delivery; outward travel adds carrying at the step that uses it, with safe reachable props.

steps.setup: Use the familiar grippable toy and a non-slip floor. Sit where you can support it at progressively lower heights without crowding your dog, with a receiving hand and rewards ready.
steps.decision: A stationary pickup from a lower surface uses known take/hold/give, covered by hand delivery; traveling carries are not used until the next step.

steps.setup: Clear a short straight area and place the familiar toy close in front of you on non-slip flooring. Prepare your receiving-hand finish and rewards; no throw or fast chase is needed.
steps.decision: The short outward retrieve now explicitly requires carrying at the step that introduces travel.

BOX.title: Put toys in a basket
BOX.previousSharedSetup: Low stable basket; large safe toys; no food competition.
BOX.sharedSetupReview: Basket release can start from hand delivery; floor collection adds the retrieve only where it is needed.

steps.setup: Secure a low wide basket beneath your receiving-hand position. Have one familiar large safe toy and rewards ready, with other animals separated and a clear view of the opening.
steps.decision: Hand delivery transfers to a basket release independently; adding floor pickup and travel explicitly requires retrieve.

steps.setup: Keep the familiar basket stable on non-slip flooring and place one safe toy about a step away. Clear the short route to its opening and have rewards accessible beside the basket.
steps.decision: Hand delivery transfers to a basket release independently; adding floor pickup and travel explicitly requires retrieve.

SEARCH.title: Easy food search
SEARCH.previousSharedSetup: Single dog; suitable food portion; no swallowing packaging or unsafe puzzles.
SEARCH.sharedSetupReview: Simple safe visible food placements precede mild concealment; this is enjoyable exploration, not a clinical anxiety intervention.

steps.setup: Separate other animals and choose a small clean search area. Prepare a suitable food portion on a flat towel or open shallow containers that cannot be swallowed; keep packaging and unsafe puzzles out of reach.
steps.decision: Visible food investigation precedes tiny partly hidden searches; no wait or target is necessary.

steps.setup: Choose a tiny clear search area with one stable harmless object. Prepare a single easy food hide partly in view, with other animals separated and immediate access to reveal it if needed.
steps.decision: Visible food investigation precedes tiny partly hidden searches; no wait or target is necessary.

TUG.title: Gentle tug with a release
TUG.previousSharedSetup: Suitable large toy; no pain, guarding, jumping, or suspended pulling.
TUG.sharedSetupReview: Mutual low-force play and willing release are appropriate for dogs that enjoy them; avoid forced grip, high movement or guarding tests.

steps.setup: Choose a suitable large intact tug toy and a level non-slip area. Keep the toy at comfortable neck height and rewards ready for an easy trade; skip for pain, guarding or rising tension.
steps.decision: A rewarded release is used to end gentle play safely, followed by the short game-ending routine.

steps.setup: Prepare the familiar toy and rewarding release, plus a ready quiet activity or resting place. Have a safe place to put the toy after release and keep play space clear of jumping or suspended pulling. Keep play low and gentle; skip for mouth or neck discomfort.
steps.decision: A rewarded release is used to end gentle play safely, followed by the short game-ending routine.

SPIN.title: Small comfortable spin
SPIN.previousSharedSetup: Non-slip surface; skip for pain, dizziness, or mobility concerns.
SPIN.sharedSetupReview: Use a broad comfortable floor turn and fade lures; skip repetitive or tight turns for dogs with discomfort.

steps.setup: Clear a broad turning space on a non-slip floor and have a small reward ready at nose height. Begin with the dog comfortably standing; skip for pain, dizziness or mobility concerns.
steps.decision: A comfortable broad turn precedes fading the lure; reverse direction is optional and separate.

steps.setup: Use the same broad clear turning space, with the guiding hand empty and rewards separate. Choose the familiar direction first and enough room to reset to a natural stand. Skip if turning is uncomfortable.
steps.decision: A comfortable broad turn precedes fading the lure; reverse direction is optional and separate.

PAW.title: Offer a paw
PAW.previousSharedSetup: Dog comfortable lifting a paw; no grabbing or shaking the leg.
PAW.sharedSetupReview: A low voluntary offer does not authorize paw restraint for care; maintain balance, brief contact and prompt reward.

steps.setup: Use a non-slip floor and a comfortable balanced starting position. Keep a low open palm beside one front paw and rewards separate; no food-filled fist or physical paw placement is needed.
steps.decision: A voluntary low paw offer precedes cue transfer; no restraint or forced limb placement.

steps.setup: Prepare the familiar low palm target below the dog's elbow, with non-slip footing and rewards ready. Leave space to lower your hand promptly and for the foot to return freely to the floor.
steps.decision: A voluntary low paw offer precedes cue transfer; no restraint or forced limb placement.

PULL.title: Tug a rope handle
PULL.previousSharedSetup: Large intact rope handle, supervised; no mouth pain or guarding. Remove ropes after practice.
PULL.sharedSetupReview: Use an intact safe handle, negligible resistance and prompt reward after marking; do not add a release demand before the promised reward.

steps.setup: Choose a large intact rope handle without loops that could catch feet or neck. Sit at comfortable mouth height with rewards and an easy drop trade ready; supervise and remove the rope afterward.
steps.decision: A terminal marker promises prompt reward without an extra release command as a hidden requirement.

steps.setup: Use the same safe rope handle on non-slip footing, with room for one tiny backward weight shift. Hold it lightly and prepare a release reward; do not attach it to resistance yet. Skip for mouth or neck pain or item guarding.
steps.decision: Do not mark the pull and then require another response before delivering the promised reward.

steps.setup: Secure the handle to a lightweight stable training hinge or board that moves very easily. Check that its swing cannot strike the dog, clear pinch points, and prepare rewards; avoid unstable furniture. Skip for mouth or neck pain or item guarding.
steps.decision: Take and drop support gentle rope grip, tiny resistance and easy board movement; the refrigerator is a later independent transfer.

NAMECTX.title: Name response in new settings
NAMECTX.previousSharedSetup: Record each context separately; this does not change the original name-learning status.
NAMECTX.sharedSetupReview: Rebuild name response in specified easy new settings; a response in one context does not certify attention around fear or high distraction.

steps.setup: Choose a second quiet familiar room, clear of competing activity. Begin close to your dog with rewards accessible beside you and only a small comfortable angle away.
steps.decision: The original name turn transfers to another quiet room, outdoors and then a mild ordinary distraction.

steps.setup: Select a quiet fenced yard or check a comfortable secure harness/lead setup. Start nearby with generous rewards and an easy sniffing break available, away from traffic or trigger activity.
steps.decision: The original name turn transfers to another quiet room, outdoors and then a mild ordinary distraction.

steps.setup: Recreate the successful setting and choose one mild controllable distraction, such as a familiar adult moving far away. Agree on a stop signal and keep distance, rewards and retreat ready.
steps.decision: The original name turn transfers to another quiet room, outdoors and then a mild ordinary distraction.

RECALLCTX.title: Recall in a new safe setting
RECALLCTX.previousSharedSetup: Long line on a comfortable harness; secure area; no line wrapped around hands or neck. Use a securely enclosed area or a safely managed long line on comfortable fitted equipment. Start with equipment comfort separately if needed; never attach a long line to the neck or allow a hard stop.
RECALLCTX.sharedSetupReview: Use enclosure or a safely managed line on suitable body equipment; increase context difficulty without reeling in or hard stops.

steps.setup: Choose a secure enclosure or a slack long line on a comfortable fitted harness, never the neck. Clear snag hazards, keep line away from hands and legs, and start close with generous rewards.
steps.decision: The indoor recall transfers; comfortable fitted long-line equipment is a safety condition, not an extra obedience prerequisite.

steps.setup: Keep the successful enclosure or safely managed long-line setup. Select either a slightly longer clear approach or a mild ordinary sniffing opportunity, with the other feature easy and no road, wildlife or frightening trigger nearby.
steps.decision: A fluent indoor recall is the learned component; safe enclosure or comfortable line equipment is checked directly.

MATCTX.title: Mat comfort in another place
MATCTX.previousSharedSetup: Start with a quiet room, not a busy cafe or trigger-filled park.
MATCTX.sharedSetupReview: Transfer stationing to a new room before adding quiet rest; the rest prerequisite belongs at the step that uses it.

steps.setup: Lay the familiar mat on a non-slip floor in another quiet room. Start beside it with rewards ready and space for an easy approach and exit, without a long stay planned.
steps.decision: Moving the mat cue to a new room precedes resting and need not wait for settled duration.

steps.setup: Place the familiar mat in the successful new quiet spot and sit nearby with quiet rewards. Keep an open exit; prepare only a small ordinary household movement if the restful interval is already comfortable.
steps.decision: The quiet-rest component is required at the step that actually transfers it.

WALKCTX.title: Loose walking in another place
WALKCTX.previousSharedSetup: Secure comfortable equipment; broad paths and exits.
WALKCTX.sharedSetupReview: Transfer the learned slack-lead action in easier new settings; equipment and optional exits do not become unrelated grade gates.

steps.setup: Choose a quiet nearby place such as the yard edge, with broad footing and a clear exit. Check comfortable secure equipment and rewards at your side; keep a sniff-break area available.
steps.decision: Transfer uses loose walking; a turn-away remains a useful optional exit, not part of the taught walking action.

steps.setup: Use the successful short route and identify one modest change in step count or ordinary activity. Check secure equipment and your exit route, with rewards ready and real triggers outside the exercise.
steps.decision: Loose walking transfers directly to an easy new setting; a turn-away remains an optional exit aid.

KEEP.title: Maintain skills and review changes
KEEP.previousSharedSetup: Select a few useful skills; do not retest everything in one session.
KEEP.sharedSetupReview: Refresh only observed exact criteria and contexts; absent logs do not establish forgetting, and changed fear calls for assessment rather than drilling.

steps.setup: Select one familiar useful skill and an optional enjoyable activity. Prepare only their usual safe equipment in an easy setting, with rewards ready and enough time for a brief relaxed session.
steps.decision: A refresher does not justify promoting every stage or broader context without observing its criterion.

steps.setup: Have your session log and comparable earlier observations open. Identify the same trigger and setting before reviewing; no new exposure or obedience test is needed, and unknown measurements can stay blank.
steps.decision: A maintenance routine precedes a supported review of comparable journal records; no all-catalog completion gate.

BOW.title: Take a little bow
BOW.previousSharedSetup: Healthy comfortable movement on a non-slip floor. Capture a natural stretch; skip for pain, stiffness, or balance concerns.
BOW.sharedSetupReview: An optional brief comfortable shape is not a stretch prescription; no pushing, prolonged holding or training through stiffness.

steps.setup: Choose an ordinary relaxed transition from rest on non-slip flooring. Keep a reward quietly accessible and enough space around your dog for a natural stretch; do not wake or provoke them.
steps.decision: Natural comfortable stretch capture precedes shaping a small offered dip, then naming; no forced positioning.

steps.setup: Prepare a broad non-slip patch during a comfortable playful moment. Sit or stand where your empty hand can signal without touching the body, with rewards separate and room to stand again.
steps.decision: Natural comfortable stretch capture precedes shaping a small offered dip, then naming; no forced positioning.

steps.setup: Use the same comfortable non-slip area and familiar empty-hand gesture. Have rewards ready and plan only a few brief turns; skip for stiffness, imbalance or reluctance rather than preparing a held stretch.
steps.decision: Natural comfortable stretch capture precedes shaping a small offered dip, then naming; no forced positioning.

MIDDLE.title: Stand between your legs
MIDDLE.previousSharedSetup: Only if the dog fits with generous clearance and the handler is steady; otherwise use a cone game.
MIDDLE.sharedSetupReview: Reward a voluntary comfortable position between still legs with an open exit; no squeezing or body blocking.

steps.setup: Check that your steady wide stance leaves generous clearance for the dog's whole body. Clear a straight non-slip route through and beyond your legs, with an empty target hand and rewards ready; use cones if clearance is inadequate.
steps.decision: The actual guiding hand target supports comfortable passage, then a brief middle position.

steps.setup: Use the familiar roomy stance with your feet still and a clear forward exit. Keep rewards accessible at natural forward head height; neither participant should need to balance awkwardly or close the gap.
steps.decision: The actual guiding hand target supports comfortable passage, then a brief middle position.

WEAVE.title: A slow figure eight
WEAVE.previousSharedSetup: Generous body clearance and a steady handler; wide curves only. Cone figure eights are an alternative.
WEAVE.sharedSetupReview: Each separate leg-loop can be taught in parallel; joining them needs both and enough room for broad comfortable movement.

steps.setup: Use a steady wide stance on non-slip footing with generous space around one leg. Have the familiar target hand and separate rewards ready; use a cone instead if body clearance is tight.
steps.decision: Each loop can start from the same comfortable pass independently; joining the eight requires both loops.

steps.setup: Clear an equally broad arc around the other leg, with your feet steady. Prepare the other empty target hand and accessible rewards without arranging a faster linked sequence yet.
steps.decision: Each loop can start from the same comfortable pass independently; joining the eight requires both loops.

steps.setup: Prepare both familiar broad loops on non-slip flooring, with ample exit space and still feet. Keep both target hands available and rewards accessible for a halfway reward if needed.
steps.decision: Each loop can start from the same comfortable pass independently; joining the eight requires both loops.

NOSEBALL.title: Roll a ball with the nose
NOSEBALL.previousSharedSetup: A lightweight ball far too large to swallow; clear flat non-slip floor; no hard or tiny balls.
NOSEBALL.sharedSetupReview: Nose contact precedes a small slow floor roll; use an oversized safe ball without frantic chasing or ingestion risk.

steps.setup: Choose a light smooth ball far too large to swallow and a clear non-slip area. Hold it still just below natural nose height, with rewards separate; avoid hard balls or small detachable parts.
steps.decision: Ball contact precedes a gentle movable nudge, then a named short roll; generic object targeting is optional.

steps.setup: Use the familiar oversized light ball on flat non-slip flooring. Position your foot to prevent an uncontrolled roll, clear a small space ahead and have rewards ready for a tiny nudge.
steps.decision: Ball contact precedes a gentle movable nudge, then a named short roll; generic object targeting is optional.

steps.setup: Clear a short flat non-slip rolling lane and use the familiar oversized ball. Keep rewards nearby and a safe way to stop and reset the ball yourself; no chase or fast play is planned.
steps.decision: Ball contact precedes a gentle movable nudge, then a named short roll; generic object targeting is optional.

BOWL.title: Dog bowling
BOWL.previousSharedSetup: Known ball push; two or three soft pins that fall quietly; no chewable small pieces.
BOWL.sharedSetupReview: Use a broad slow ball nudge toward lightweight pins; keep noise and movement easy and avoid any athletic or anxiety-treatment claim.

steps.setup: Place one soft quiet-falling pin just beyond the familiar oversized ball on a straight non-slip lane. Remove chewable fragments and clear space for you to reset equipment, with rewards ready.
steps.decision: The known cued ball roll is transferred to one soft pin before a small cluster.

steps.setup: Arrange two or three familiar soft quiet pins in a close wide cluster beyond a short straight ball lane. Check all pieces are too large to swallow and have rewards accessible for each reset.
steps.decision: The known cued ball roll is transferred to one soft pin before a small cluster.

GOAL.title: Score a gentle goal
GOAL.previousSharedSetup: Two widely spaced soft markers and a known oversized ball; no nets or entanglement hazards.
GOAL.sharedSetupReview: Target and direction changes are taught gradually with a safe large ball; goal success is a specific game, not general intelligence.

steps.setup: Place two soft stable markers widely apart just beyond the familiar oversized ball. Clear a short non-slip lane and the far side; leave out nets, cords or entangling equipment and have rewards ready.
steps.decision: The known ball roll is directed through an easy broad goal, then named separately.

steps.setup: Use the same close wide goal and clear rolling lane, with rewards accessible. Keep the start position familiar initially; prepare only a small offset if the established game is comfortable.
steps.decision: The known ball roll is directed through an easy broad goal, then named separately.

HIGHFIVE.title: Low high five
HIGHFIVE.previousSharedSetup: A stable comfortable position; hand kept below the dog’s elbow, with no paw pulling.
HIGHFIVE.sharedSetupReview: Adapt a known low paw offer without stretching, impact or holding the limb; skip if balance or scratching is a concern.

steps.setup: Use comfortable balanced footing and the familiar paw starting position. Keep an empty palm upright but below elbow height, with rewards separate and space for the paw to return freely.
steps.decision: A voluntary paw offer is the action transferred to a low upright palm.

steps.setup: Prepare the familiar low upright palm target and non-slip footing. Keep rewards ready and the target hand easy to lower immediately; no high lift or held paw is planned.
steps.decision: A voluntary paw offer is the action transferred to a low upright palm.

WAVE.title: A little wave
WAVE.previousSharedSetup: Comfortable balanced position and known low high five; no repeated high paw lifts.
WAVE.sharedSetupReview: A small offered paw lift is sufficient before naming; a completed high-five is an unnecessary detour and height is not the goal.

steps.setup: Begin on non-slip flooring in a comfortable balanced position with a familiar small paw offer. Prepare a low empty palm and separate rewards; a finished high five is not required.
steps.decision: A small offered paw lift is sufficient; turning the palm into a high five is an optional detour.

steps.setup: Use the same stable surface and comfortable low invitation, with rewards accessible. Leave space between hand and paw without prompting an overreach; one small lift is enough for a turn.
steps.decision: A small paw offer is sufficient; a completed high-five detour is unnecessary.

POSE.title: A comfortable photo pose
POSE.previousSharedSetup: Use a known comfortable sit or stand; no costumes, forced handling, flash, or startling props.
POSE.sharedSetupReview: Teach phone comfort separately; take the quick silent photo before the terminal marker and promptly reward without extending the hold.

steps.setup: Choose a familiar comfortable sit or stand area with non-slip footing. Hold the phone down, disable flash and startling sounds, and keep rewards ready; leave costumes and props out.
steps.decision: A comfortable offered position and phone presence precede naming the pose and one silent photograph.

steps.setup: Use the familiar pose area and check the camera is silent with flash off. Keep phone movements small, rewards accessible and an open release route; prepare just one brief photo opportunity.
steps.decision: The photograph precedes the terminal marker so continued stillness is not required after a promised reward.

TOYNAME.title: Give one toy a name
TOYNAME.previousSharedSetup: One safe favorite toy in a quiet room; this experiment is optional and does not test intelligence.
TOYNAME.sharedSetupReview: Pair one toy label through enjoyable interaction; ordinary targeting remains valid without reliable object-name learning.

steps.setup: Choose one safe familiar toy and a short distinct label in advance. Put other toys away and prepare a quiet open play area and the reward or game your dog already enjoys.
steps.decision: Playful label pairing is independent of retrieval; a clear approach is an accepted response.

steps.setup: Place only the familiar named toy on a clear nearby floor patch. Keep rewards ready and your pickup invitation available, with no extra objects or hidden location changes.
steps.decision: Playful label pairing is independent of retrieval; a clear approach is an accepted response.

TWOOBJECT.title: An optional two-toy choice
TWOOBJECT.previousSharedSetup: Two safe familiar toys with distinct labels; neutral body position; optional helper to place objects.
TWOOBJECT.sharedSetupReview: Teach each familiar toy association before mixed choices, with swapped locations and neutral humans; avoid vocabulary or intelligence guarantees.

steps.setup: Choose the second safe distinct toy and its own short label. Put the first toy away, clear a small play area, and prepare a familiar enjoyable game; each association is practiced separately initially.
steps.decision: Second-toy pairing is independent; mixed choices require both familiar label associations before cue-control checks.

steps.setup: Place the two familiar safe toys a short equal distance from a central handler position on a clear floor. Keep rewards hidden and hands still; avoid leaning or looking toward the intended answer.
steps.decision: Second-toy pairing is independent; mixed choices require both familiar label associations before cue-control checks.

steps.setup: Arrange a helper to swap the two familiar toys at equal distances while you stay centered. Have a simple choice record ready, rewards hidden and a mixed request order without a predictable side pattern.
steps.decision: Second-toy pairing is independent; mixed choices require both familiar label associations before cue-control checks.

CARDS.title: Respond to picture cue cards
CARDS.previousSharedSetup: Two large distinct cards, a comfortable known sit or stand, and a known nose touch. Hold the card in one hand and keep the other empty target palm available in exactly the same position for both symbols; use a comfortable reset between trials.
CARDS.sharedSetupReview: Keep the target hand available in both symbol conditions and reset between turns; otherwise gestures or opportunity confound visual cue claims.

steps.setup: Two large distinct cards, a comfortable known sit or stand, and a known nose touch. Hold the card in one hand and keep the other empty target palm available in exactly the same position for both symbols; use a comfortable reset between trials.
steps.decision: Hold the target hand and posture constant across both symbols; otherwise hand presentation can be the actual cue.

steps.setup: Two large distinct cards, a comfortable known sit or stand, and a known nose touch. Hold the card in one hand and keep the other empty target palm available in exactly the same position for both symbols; use a comfortable reset between trials.
steps.decision: The nose-touch opportunity must be available in both conditions, not only when the stripe card appears.

steps.setup: Two large distinct cards, a comfortable known sit or stand, and a known nose touch. Hold the card in one hand and keep the other empty target palm available in exactly the same position for both symbols; use a comfortable reset between trials.
steps.decision: Only transfer from the old action cues under comparable conditions supports a visual-discrimination interpretation.

CROSSPAW.title: Rest with crossed front paws
CROSSPAW.previousSharedSetup: A broad soft non-slip surface, comfortable down and a small willing paw offer. Skip if shoulders, elbows or wrists are uncomfortable; no held or forced crossing.
CROSSPAW.sharedSetupReview: Offer only a tiny comfortable placement without limb manipulation; optional appearance does not justify strain or a prolonged posture.

steps.setup: Provide a broad soft non-slip surface and wait for a comfortable voluntary down. Keep an empty receiving hand low near one front paw and rewards separate; skip for shoulder, elbow or wrist discomfort.
steps.decision: Comfortable down and a low paw offer are the actual positioning components of a tiny voluntary crossing.

steps.setup: Use the familiar soft surface and small inward invitation, with space for both forelegs to move freely. Keep rewards accessible and the receiving hand easy to lower; no limb is held or positioned. Skip for shoulder, elbow or wrist discomfort.
steps.decision: Make the reward explicit and accept movement after marking rather than extending a strained pose.

TILT.title: A little head tilt
TILT.previousSharedSetup: Quiet familiar surroundings; capture only natural comfortable movement. No startling noises or repeated unusual sounds to provoke it.
TILT.sharedSetupReview: Capture only a naturally comfortable small head movement; avoid inducing repeated neck strain or interpreting a tilt as comprehension.

steps.setup: Choose a quiet familiar moment of ordinary friendly interaction, with a reward readily available. Leave the head free and avoid unusual repeated sounds; no tilt needs to be produced for the session.
steps.decision: Naturally offered comfortable movement is captured and then named; no noise or posture prerequisite.

steps.setup: Use the familiar comfortable interaction where a small tilt has occurred naturally. Keep rewards accessible and your posture neutral, with no props, startling sounds or expectation of a larger held angle.
steps.decision: Naturally offered comfortable movement is captured and then named; no noise or posture prerequisite.

SHAKEOFF.title: Shake off on cue
SHAKEOFF.previousSharedSetup: Capture ordinary comfortable shakes only. Do not use stress, water sprays, restraint or irritating objects to produce them.
SHAKEOFF.sharedSetupReview: Capture ordinary spontaneous shaking without provoking stress, wetting or restraint; it is not a guaranteed emotional reset.

steps.setup: Keep a reward available during an ordinary comfortable transition from rest. Leave enough room around your dog for free whole-body movement; do not add water, restraint or irritating props.
steps.decision: Natural ordinary shakes are captured before naming; stress must never be manufactured to elicit them.

steps.setup: Use the same naturally predictable comfortable context, with a reward ready and space to move. No wetting, stress or repeated prompts are part of the setup; the cue is optional if no shake follows.
steps.decision: Natural ordinary shakes are captured before naming; stress must never be manufactured to elicit them.

CIRCLEME.title: Circle around the handler
CIRCLEME.previousSharedSetup: Open non-slip space and a steady standing or seated handler; generous clearance, no moving feet or tight curves.
CIRCLEME.sharedSetupReview: Use a broad floor route around a stationary handler and fade guidance; avoid tripping, tight turns or pulling.

steps.setup: Stand steadily or sit in a stable chair with broad non-slip space around you. Clear the first half-loop of obstacles, keep target hands empty and rewards accessible, and leave feet still.
steps.decision: The known hand target guides broad independent halves before joining the loop around a stationary person.

steps.setup: Clear the whole broad route around your steady body or chair, including the finish away from your feet. Prepare both familiar target hands and rewards for a halfway delivery if useful.
steps.decision: The known hand target guides broad independent halves before joining the loop around a stationary person.

UNROLL.title: Unroll a short mat
UNROLL.previousSharedSetup: A lightweight non-slip mat with a very loose broad roll, no straps, food hidden inside or material the dog chews. Supervise and remove after practice.
UNROLL.sharedSetupReview: Keep the towel light, clean and flat with accessible rewards; no wrapping, chewing fabric or forced crawling.

steps.setup: On non-slip flooring, secure most of a lightweight mat flat and loosely roll only a few inches at the front. Prepare the familiar large nose target and separate rewards; remove straps and skip fabric chewers.
steps.decision: Known object nose targeting transfers to a loose roll, then one or two gentle nudges; ball pushing is unnecessary.

steps.setup: Set up the same short, very loose roll with secure footing and clear hands. Have the familiar pad available to reduce gradually, rewards separate, and somewhere to remove the mat after one or two nudges. Skip if the dog chews fabric.
steps.decision: Known object nose targeting transfers to a loose roll, then one or two gentle nudges; ball pushing is unnecessary.

LEFTRIGHT.title: Choose left or right targets
LEFTRIGHT.previousSharedSetup: Two identical broad flat targets, equal short distances on each side. Directions are from the dog’s starting orientation, with no reading or reasoning claim.
LEFTRIGHT.sharedSetupReview: Teach each easy direction separately, then mixed neutral requests; changing handler position or viewpoint requires new practice.

steps.setup: Place one familiar flat mat a comfortable step to your dog's left from a consistent forward-facing start. Put the right target away and keep rewards accessible without leaning toward the mat.
steps.decision: Each target-direction pairing uses known mat arrival independently; mixed choices require both, with fixed start orientation.

steps.setup: Put the left mat away and place one familiar flat target a step to the dog's right. Keep the same forward-facing starting orientation and rewards separate; this pairing can be practiced independently.
steps.decision: Each target-direction pairing uses known mat arrival independently; mixed choices require both, with fixed start orientation.

steps.setup: Place two identical broad flat targets at equal short distances either side of the usual forward-facing start. Stand centered with neutral hands and gaze, rewards hidden and a simple response record ready.
steps.decision: Each target-direction pairing uses known mat arrival independently; mixed choices require both, with fixed start orientation.

NOD.title: A small nose-target nod
NOD.previousSharedSetup: A broad safe target, natural neck range and brief turns. No repeated bobbing, head pressure or exaggerated flexion.
NOD.sharedSetupReview: Capture a tiny comfortable head motion without pressing or stretching; this is an optional trained movement, not yes/no comprehension.

steps.setup: Prepare the familiar broad safe nose target and rewards separate. Stand at natural head height in a quiet area, with room for a second target position only slightly lower; skip neck stiffness.
steps.decision: Known object targeting guides two very close natural head heights before a small cue transfer.

steps.setup: Use the familiar target and the same tiny lower-to-neutral range. Keep rewards accessible and plan one or two brief turns, with no head pressure or equipment that could restrict movement. Skip for neck stiffness.
steps.decision: Known object targeting guides two very close natural head heights before a small cue transfer.

POINT.title: Follow a pointing gesture
POINT.previousSharedSetup: Two identical broad flat targets in a quiet space. Handler points without leaning over or crowding; this is learned cue-following rather than a claim about reasoning.
POINT.sharedSetupReview: Use clear target positions and neutral body language; trained directional choices do not establish understanding of arbitrary human intentions.

steps.setup: Place one familiar broad flat mat a step away in a quiet room. Stand where your arm gesture is comfortably visible without leaning over the dog, with rewards separate and a clear approach.
steps.decision: Known mat arrival transfers to a gesture with one target before two-target mixed choices; directional words are independent.

steps.setup: Place two identical flat mats equally near on non-slip flooring. Prepare a central starting position, still feet and neutral gaze, with rewards accessible and space for one clear pointing gesture.
steps.decision: Known mat arrival transfers to a gesture with one target before two-target mixed choices; directional words are independent.

BACK.title: Back up a few steps
BACK.previousSharedSetup: Flat non-slip space with an unobstructed route; no narrow chute, leash pressure, or approach into the dog.
BACK.sharedSetupReview: Reward a small voluntary weight shift and step with an open route; no body pressure, narrow trapping channel or backward distance quota.

steps.setup: Choose an open non-slip patch with clear space behind your comfortably standing dog. Stand still without crowding them and keep rewards ready at natural head height; no wall, narrow chute or lead pressure is needed.
steps.decision: A voluntary backward weight shift precedes one named step and then two or three; no body pressure.

steps.setup: Use the same level open area with at least one comfortable footstep of clear space behind the dog. Keep your own feet still and rewards accessible without leaning into their route.
steps.decision: A voluntary backward weight shift precedes one named step and then two or three; no body pressure.

steps.setup: Check a level non-slip route behind your dog for several slow steps, well away from edges or furniture. Stand still with rewards ready; keep the area open rather than creating a narrow backward channel.
steps.decision: A voluntary backward weight shift precedes one named step and then two or three; no body pressure.

CONE.title: Go around a cone
CONE.previousSharedSetup: A stable soft cone or broad safe object; clear non-slip space.
CONE.sharedSetupReview: A wide stationary floor marker supports gentle direction learning; safety depends on footing and comfortable turning rather than speed.

steps.setup: Place one stable soft cone in open non-slip space a short distance away. Clear a broad walking arc around it, prepare the familiar empty hand target and keep rewards at the far side accessible.
steps.decision: The known hand target actually guides a broad arc before naming and joining the loop.

steps.setup: Use the same nearby stable cone and roomy loop, with no obstacles at the finish. Keep your guiding hand empty and rewards ready for an easy halfway delivery if needed.
steps.decision: The known hand target actually guides a broad arc before naming and joining the loop.

CONEEIGHT.title: Figure eight around two markers
CONEEIGHT.previousSharedSetup: Two soft stable markers spaced generously apart; comfortable walking only.
CONEEIGHT.sharedSetupReview: Teach individual broad loops before combining them; keep distance and turns comfortable without repetitive athletic demands.

steps.setup: Place two familiar soft stable markers far apart on non-slip flooring, allowing broad ordinary walking curves. Keep the target hand and rewards ready, with space to pause between separate loops.
steps.decision: Known separate cone loops precede their broad connection; no leg weave is required.

steps.setup: Recreate the two broad familiar loops and clear the center route between them. Have rewards accessible at the center and both hand invitations available; no tight weaving or faster pace is planned.
steps.decision: Known separate cone loops precede their broad connection; no leg weave is required.

FEET.title: Front paws on a flat target
FEET.previousSharedSetup: A broad non-slip mat lying flat, with no raised or unstable platform.
FEET.sharedSetupReview: A flat secured mat teaches front-paw placement; elevation or unstable equipment is deliberately outside this sequence.

steps.setup: Lay a broad non-slip mat flat in an open room. Leave room for voluntary approaches and a small reset away, with rewards ready and no raised edge or wobbling equipment.
steps.decision: Direct front-foot contact precedes two-front-foot targeting, then the cue, all at floor level.

steps.setup: Use the same broad floor-level mat with enough width for both front paws. Keep rewards accessible at natural head height and clear floor around the rear feet and exit.
steps.decision: Direct front-foot contact precedes two-front-foot targeting, then the cue, all at floor level.

steps.setup: Place the familiar mat flat in its successful location. Keep the invitation hand empty and rewards separate, with a clear approach and release route; no raised or unstable surface is included.
steps.decision: Direct front-foot contact precedes two-front-foot targeting, then the cue, all at floor level.

HOOP.title: Walk through a floor-level hoop
HOOP.previousSharedSetup: A very wide smooth hoop held stationary with its bottom resting on the floor; no collars or tags that can snag.
HOOP.sharedSetupReview: Use a broad floor-level opening with optional guidance, not jumping; remove duplicate wording without changing the criterion.

steps.setup: Hold a very wide smooth hoop stationary with its bottom on the floor. Clear the route through and around it, check that equipment or tags cannot snag, and prepare the familiar target and rewards.
steps.decision: Exploring an opening and following a small optional lure can be taught directly; a finished hand target unnecessarily blocks exploration.

steps.setup: Use the familiar wide stationary hoop at floor level with clear approach and exit space. Keep any guiding hand empty and rewards ready beyond the opening; no jumping, narrowing or raised height is planned. Check tags and equipment cannot snag.
steps.decision: Remove duplicated wording without changing the exercise.

TUNNEL.title: Explore an open tunnel
TUNNEL.previousSharedSetup: A wide rigid/open-ended dog tunnel secured against rolling; start extremely short or fully open. A helper may steady equipment, never hold the dog.
TUNNEL.sharedSetupReview: An open broad short floor-level passage is voluntary; never trap or push the dog through, and skip if confinement is uncomfortable.

steps.setup: Secure a wide rigid open-ended tunnel against rolling, using its shortest or fully open form. Keep the interior bright and far end visible, with rewards outside and plenty of room to walk away.
steps.decision: Open entrance comfort precedes a tiny straight pass and its cue; no hoop or jumping prerequisite.

steps.setup: Set the familiar tunnel to its shortest bright straight opening and check both ends are clear. Keep a reward hand visible just beyond the exit; a helper may steady equipment without touching the dog.
steps.decision: Open entrance comfort precedes a tiny straight pass and its cue; no hoop or jumping prerequisite.

steps.setup: Use the same stable bright straight tunnel and obvious exits. Keep rewards accessible beyond the far end and any extra length minimal; avoid dark, curved, long or collapsible fabric arrangements.
steps.decision: Open entrance comfort precedes a tiny straight pass and its cue; no hoop or jumping prerequisite.

REAR.title: Rear feet on a flat target
REAR.previousSharedSetup: A long broad non-slip mat, lying flat with no raised platform. Comfortable ordinary movement only.
REAR.sharedSetupReview: Tiny voluntary rear-foot awareness on flat targets is optional; avoid lifting limbs or claiming rehabilitation benefits.

steps.setup: Lay a long broad non-slip mat flat across an open walking route. Clear the approach and forward exit, with rewards ready at natural head height; no paw placement or rearward pushing is needed.
steps.decision: Forward passes directly shape rear-foot contact before pausing and naming a flat target position.

steps.setup: Use a floor-level mat long enough for comfortable rear-foot contact after front feet move beyond it. Check balanced footing and a clear forward exit, with rewards accessible without stretching the dog.
steps.decision: Forward passes directly shape rear-foot contact before pausing and naming a flat target position.

steps.setup: Keep the familiar long mat flat on a straight roomy route. Prepare the known slow approach and nearby reward position, with an open forward release; no raised perch or balance equipment is included.
steps.decision: Forward passes directly shape rear-foot contact before pausing and naming a flat target position.

SIDESTEP.title: Take a sideways step
SIDESTEP.previousSharedSetup: Open non-slip space with room to move away. Work both directions separately without demanding symmetry or using body pressure.
SIDESTEP.sharedSetupReview: Reward small lateral weight changes without crowding; stop for awkward movement or strain rather than demanding precise footwork.

steps.setup: Stand at an angle beside your comfortably standing dog on a broad non-slip floor. Leave generous space on both sides and keep rewards accessible without stepping into the dog or twisting their head.
steps.decision: A voluntary lateral foot shift is shaped into a short side step without crowding or requiring backward walking.

steps.setup: Use the same open non-slip area and choose one comfortable direction for this turn. Keep your feet still, rewards ready and room for both front and rear feet to adjust freely.
steps.decision: A voluntary lateral foot shift is shaped into a short side step without crowding or requiring backward walking.

PIVOT.title: Move the rear feet around a flat target
PIVOT.previousSharedSetup: A broad non-slip floor target, open space and healthy comfortable movement. No raised perch, tight rotations or long repetitions.
PIVOT.sharedSetupReview: Use broad tiny comfortable alignment changes on safe low or flat support; no pressure, speed or exercise prescription.

steps.setup: Lay a broad familiar front-foot target flat on non-slip flooring. Clear generous space around the rear feet and keep rewards at natural head height, with an open route off the mat.
steps.decision: The front-feet target is the actual fixed component while small rear-foot adjustments form a short arc.

steps.setup: Use the same broad flat target and clear rear-foot arc, with rewards accessible near natural head height. Prepare only one or two small steps and an easy release, without tight rotation or a full circle.
steps.decision: The front-feet target is the actual fixed component while small rear-foot adjustments form a short arc.

UNDER.title: Walk under a roomy obstacle
UNDER.previousSharedSetup: A stable open table or broad arch with generous head and body clearance, no low bars, dangling objects or enclosed dead ends.
UNDER.sharedSetupReview: Begin with a wide high stationary opening and free exits; avoid squeezing, ducking pressure or handler movement over the dog.

steps.setup: Choose a stable high table or broad arch with generous head and body clearance. Remove dangling items and clear both ends and the route around it, with rewards accessible; no crawling or dead end is involved.
steps.decision: Open overhead-space exploration directly precedes a roomy walking pass; a tunnel is a different task.

steps.setup: Use the familiar high stable opening and clear a straight natural-height walking path. Keep the invitation hand empty and rewards ready beyond the exit, with room to reset away from the structure.
steps.decision: Open overhead-space exploration directly precedes a roomy walking pass; a tunnel is a different task.

POLES.title: Step over ground poles
POLES.previousSharedSetup: Two or three broad visible poles that cannot roll, completely on the floor, with generous spacing for this dog. Non-slip footing and comfortable movement; no jumping or fitness prescription.
POLES.sharedSetupReview: Widely spaced floor markers support slow comfortable routes; this is not agility weave-pole conditioning.

steps.setup: Secure one broad visible pole flat on level non-slip ground so it cannot roll. Clear a gentle approach and far-side reward space; use a flat strip instead if normal walking clearance is difficult.
steps.decision: One secured ground-pole crossing precedes a very short naturally spaced line, without raised obstacles.

steps.setup: Secure two familiar poles flat on non-slip ground with several natural steps between them. Check spacing for this dog and a clear finish; a third is optional only without changing ordinary gait.
steps.decision: One secured ground-pole crossing precedes a very short naturally spaced line, without raised obstacles.

SURFACE.title: Choose unfamiliar safe surfaces
SURFACE.previousSharedSetup: Clean secure non-slip textures such as rubber and tightly secured fabric on the floor. No hot, sharp, noisy unstable or painful surfaces.
SURFACE.sharedSetupReview: Introduce stable non-slip flat textures voluntarily; avoid unstable balance challenges or physical forcing.

steps.setup: Secure a small clean non-slip texture beside familiar flooring, checking for heat, sharp edges, noise or wobble. Leave the familiar side open, with rewards available for both interest and an easy retreat.
steps.decision: Voluntary single-foot contact precedes crossing a small stable texture and separately introducing another.

steps.setup: Prepare a short broad patch of the already familiar secured texture with clear familiar flooring beyond it. Keep rewards at the exit and a route around; introduce a different texture separately from the easiest arrangement.
steps.decision: Voluntary single-foot contact precedes crossing a small stable texture and separately introducing another.

OPEN.title: Open a lightweight training prop
OPEN.previousSharedSetup: A stable lightweight purpose-built practice cabinet with rounded edges, guarded hinge gaps and no latch or seal. A human controls its easy door travel. Use a non-slip floor and remove the prop and handle after supervised practice. Never use an electrical or food-storage appliance.
OPEN.sharedSetupReview: Retire refrigerator exposure and pulling; new IDs teach a human-controlled freely moving purpose-built practice door without a seal or latch.

steps.setup: A stable lightweight purpose-built practice cabinet with rounded edges, guarded hinge gaps and no latch or seal. A human controls its easy door travel. Use a non-slip floor and remove the prop and handle after supervised practice. Never use an electrical or food-storage appliance.
steps.decision: New prop context replaces appliance exposure without assuming historical refrigerator comfort transfers.

steps.setup: A stable lightweight purpose-built practice cabinet with rounded edges, guarded hinge gaps and no latch or seal. A human controls its easy door travel. Use a non-slip floor and remove the prop and handle after supervised practice. Never use an electrical or food-storage appliance. Prepare the familiar intact handle with no loop around the dog.
steps.decision: Pulling uses both door comfort and a learned gentle prop pull, without an appliance seal.

steps.setup: A stable lightweight purpose-built practice cabinet with rounded edges, guarded hinge gaps and no latch or seal. A human controls its easy door travel. Use a non-slip floor and remove the prop and handle after supervised practice. Never use an electrical or food-storage appliance. Use the same familiar handle and starting gap.
steps.decision: Cue transfer and modest starting-gap variation stay within the same low-force training prop.

CLOSE.title: Nudge a lightweight training door
CLOSE.previousSharedSetup: A stable lightweight purpose-built practice cabinet with rounded edges, guarded hinge gaps and no latch or seal. A human controls its easy door travel. Use a non-slip floor and remove the prop and handle after supervised practice. Never use an electrical or food-storage appliance.
CLOSE.sharedSetupReview: Keep gentle target and low-force prop contact, retire refrigerator closure and teach a new prop-only nudge cue without assumed historical credit.

steps.setup: A stable lightweight purpose-built practice cabinet with rounded edges, guarded hinge gaps and no latch or seal. A human controls its easy door travel. Use a non-slip floor and remove the prop and handle after supervised practice. Never use an electrical or food-storage appliance. Prepare the familiar broad secure target pad at comfortable nose height.
steps.decision: Define the lightweight door as a guarded practice prop, not a household appliance.

steps.setup: A stable lightweight purpose-built practice cabinet with rounded edges, guarded hinge gaps and no latch or seal. A human controls its easy door travel. Use a non-slip floor and remove the prop and handle after supervised practice. Never use an electrical or food-storage appliance. Place the secure broad nose target where the dog can touch without reaching into the gap.
steps.decision: Closing remains a low-force prop exercise with controlled travel, rather than an appliance job.

steps.setup: A stable lightweight purpose-built practice cabinet with rounded edges, guarded hinge gaps and no latch or seal. A human controls its easy door travel. Use a non-slip floor and remove the prop and handle after supervised practice. Never use an electrical or food-storage appliance. Keep the familiar broad target secure and the starting gap tiny.
steps.decision: A new prop-only cue record replaces refrigerator closure; completion does not certify an appliance seal.

SHELF.title: Retrieve from a low practice shelf
SHELF.previousSharedSetup: An empty robust lightweight dog-safe carrier with a broad safe grip, and a stable low open practice shelf at natural mouth height. No contents, bottles, cans, small closures, food-storage cabinet or appliance; all feet remain on the floor.
SHELF.sharedSetupReview: Keep hand delivery and reachable-surface pickup with an empty safe carrier; replace appliance access with a human-opened practice prop.

steps.setup: Prepare an empty robust lightweight carrier with a broad safe grip and no detachable pieces. Inspect it for damage; sit or stand close on a clear non-slip floor with rewards ready.
steps.decision: The hand-delivery component needs no beverage or edible contents.

steps.setup: Set the familiar empty safe carrier on a stable low open practice shelf at natural mouth height. Clear a short non-slip delivery route; all paws stay on the floor, with no appliance or deep reach.
steps.decision: Keep the existing reachable-surface pickup while making the empty training object explicit.

steps.setup: A stable lightweight purpose-built practice cabinet with rounded edges, guarded hinge gaps and no latch or seal. A human controls its easy door travel. Use a non-slip floor and remove the prop and handle after supervised practice. Never use an electrical or food-storage appliance. Secure a reachable low shelf and place the familiar empty carrier at its front edge.
steps.decision: A new safe prop context replaces access to an open refrigerator, without automatic historical credit.

BUTTON.title: Press a large quiet button
BUTTON.previousSharedSetup: A large low-force muted training button or inert practice pad; no cables, batteries, small parts, or startling sound within reach.
BUTTON.sharedSetupReview: A large secured device can cue a learned action without a small-part or electrical hazard; no language or need-reading claim follows.

steps.setup: Secure a large inert or muted low-force pad at comfortable nose height. Keep cables, batteries and small parts inaccessible, rewards separate and room to withdraw; the target must be too large to swallow.
steps.decision: Known gentle object contact transfers to a low-force pad, then depression and a separate button cue.

steps.setup: Use the familiar stable muted pad and check that it depresses with very light pressure. Keep footing secure and rewards in the other hand; choose a more sensitive pad rather than adding resistance.
steps.decision: Known gentle object contact transfers to a low-force pad, then depression and a separate button cue.

steps.setup: Place the familiar muted button in its usual stable position with rewards ready and no accessible electronics. Keep the pointing hand empty; sound or request consequences are separate lessons.
steps.decision: Known gentle object contact transfers to a low-force pad, then depression and a separate button cue.

SLIPPERS.title: Bring a designated slipper
SLIPPERS.previousSharedSetup: A clean light oversized slipper with no loose parts; skip for dogs that shred, swallow fabric, or guard items.
SLIPPERS.sharedSetupReview: Use safe dedicated props rather than small wearable parts; hand delivery precedes the floor pickup and its retrieve prerequisite.

steps.setup: Choose one clean light oversized slipper without loose parts and keep other shoes away. Have rewards and a receiving hand ready; use a safe toy instead for fabric shredders, swallowers or item guarding.
steps.decision: Hand presentation uses take and give; the floor retrieve belongs at the floor step.

steps.setup: Place the same designated safe slipper close to your feet on a clear non-slip floor. Keep the receiving hand and rewards ready, with other footwear out of reach and no long carry path yet. Skip for shredding, fabric swallowing or guarding.
steps.decision: Floor pickup and delivery now explicitly require the reusable retrieve at the point of use.

steps.setup: Put the familiar designated slipper on an obvious low mat a few clear steps away. Remove other footwear, prepare a short non-slip return route and keep rewards accessible for the hand delivery. Skip for shredding, fabric swallowing or guarding.
steps.decision: Hand take/give can begin before outward retrieving; floor pickup explicitly adds the retrieve component.

POUCH.title: Carry a little pouch
POUCH.previousSharedSetup: A soft oversized empty pouch with a broad safe grip; no straps that can loop over the head and no contents to ingest.
POUCH.sharedSetupReview: Use an empty robust safe grip first; mark delivery at the end of a hold-and-give chain, not before an extra hidden requirement.

steps.setup: Inspect a soft oversized empty pouch with a broad safe grip. Remove head-catching straps and avoid gripping zips, buckles or cords; sit at a comfortable presentation height with rewards and a receiving palm ready.
steps.decision: Mark the end of the hold-and-give sequence rather than marking a hold then delaying reward for another required action.

steps.setup: Use the familiar empty pouch and clear a short straight non-slip carry route. Keep the safe grip at comfortable mouth height, a receiving hand close and rewards ready; no added load is needed.
steps.decision: Stationary handover uses give; travel adds the carrying component only when used.

steps.setup: Only use a pouch designed to stay closed with a dog that does not shred it. Secure one protected paper note without staples or clips inside, check the safe grip, and keep the familiar short route clear.
steps.decision: Stationary handover uses give; travel adds the carrying component only when used.

MESSENGER.title: Deliver to a familiar person
MESSENGER.previousSharedSetup: Two trusted adults close together; a safe carry prop; no guarding or tension around people.
MESSENGER.sharedSetupReview: Familiar-person hand delivery precedes short travel; carrying is needed at the travel step, without enforced separation.

steps.setup: Arrange a trusted adult close beside you with an open low receiving palm and rewards. Use the familiar safe carry prop in a quiet non-slip area; no departure or stranger approach is planned.
steps.decision: Giving to a second familiar adult is independent; moving to them then requires known carrying.

steps.setup: Keep both familiar adults visible about one clear step apart. Prepare the safe prop, the helper's low receiving hand and rewards, with no obstacles or other animals on the delivery route.
steps.decision: Giving to a second familiar adult is independent; moving to them then requires known carrying.

steps.setup: Use the same familiar visible receiver, safe prop and successful short route. Have rewards at the receiving end and a quiet break ready; no unfamiliar person or forced approach is included.
steps.decision: Giving to a second familiar adult is independent; moving to them then requires known carrying.

LAUNDRY.title: Place safe cloths in a basket
LAUNDRY.previousSharedSetup: Large safe clean cloth props and a stable low basket; no socks, detergent, dirty laundry, strings, or ingestible fabric for shredders.
LAUNDRY.sharedSetupReview: Use dedicated safe light fabric and human-managed baskets; hand delivery precedes floor retrieval and no swallowing or machine access is taught.

steps.setup: Secure a broad low basket and choose one large clean designated cloth without strings or loose parts. Have rewards ready near the rim; use a toy instead for fabric chewers and keep detergent and real laundry away.
steps.decision: The close basket-release component comes first; actual floor collection adds retrieve.

steps.setup: Place the familiar safe cloth beside the stable basket's outer edge on a clear non-slip floor. Keep the opening broad, rewards accessible and the short pickup route free of other laundry. Skip for fabric chewing or swallowing.
steps.decision: The close basket-release component comes first; actual floor collection adds retrieve.

steps.setup: Set two familiar designated safe cloths a little apart near the secured low basket. Clear short visible routes and have rewards ready for separate deposits; block appliance access and keep all laundry products away. Skip for fabric chewing or swallowing.
steps.decision: The close basket-release component comes first; actual floor collection adds retrieve.

SORT.title: Two-toy tidy-up
SORT.previousSharedSetup: Two broad low baskets on distinct large markers and two safe familiar toys. Teach particular toy-to-basket pairings; avoid small labels, lids and chewable decorations.
SORT.sharedSetupReview: Teach independent toy-destination pairings before mixed choices; swap marked baskets and avoid claims of abstract material categorization.

steps.setup: Put away the second pair. Secure the first broad low basket on its distinct large marker and prepare only its familiar safe toy, with a short non-slip approach and rewards ready.
steps.decision: Two toy-destination pairs can be learned in parallel; mixed choices require both before gathering a set.

steps.setup: Put away the first pair. Prepare only the second safe toy and its broad low basket on a clearly different large marker, with a clear short route and accessible rewards.
steps.decision: Two toy-destination pairs can be learned in parallel; mixed choices require both before gathering a set.

steps.setup: Place both familiar marked baskets in clear view on non-slip flooring and offer one familiar toy at a time. Keep markers attached to their destinations, rewards hidden and your gaze neutral.
steps.decision: Two toy-destination pairs can be learned in parallel; mixed choices require both before gathering a set.

steps.setup: Set both marked baskets securely and place the two familiar toys apart on a clear floor. Leave short unobstructed carry routes and keep rewards ready; no lids, small labels or extra objects are needed.
steps.decision: Two toy-destination pairs can be learned in parallel; mixed choices require both before gathering a set.

POST.title: A two-person delivery round
POST.previousSharedSetup: Two familiar willing adults, a safe oversized pouch, broad low tray and flat starting mat. Both adults remain available; no restraint or separation distress.
POST.sharedSetupReview: Practice collection, familiar-person delivery and return as components; the original longer guide remains historical without overwriting notes.

steps.setup: Put the familiar empty oversized pouch on a stable low open tray beside the sender. Seat the trusted receiver nearby in clear view, with a non-slip delivery route and rewards at the receiving hand.
steps.decision: Collection/delivery and the empty mat return can be learned separately; joining requires both, then transfer.

steps.setup: Put the pouch aside and place the sender's familiar flat mat close to the receiver. Keep both adults visible, the return route open and rewards ready at the mat; no delivery is needed in this turn.
steps.decision: Collection/delivery and the empty mat return can be learned separately; joining requires both, then transfer.

steps.setup: Prepare the familiar tray and empty pouch at the sender, the visible nearby receiver and the sender's return mat. Clear the short non-slip round-trip route and place rewards at both ends.
steps.decision: Collection/delivery and the empty mat return can be learned separately; joining requires both, then transfer.

steps.setup: Choose only one small change in route, receiver position or familiar adult roles. Keep tray, mat and safe pouch ready, with both people visible; any note stays protected inside without staples, clips or extra load.
steps.decision: Collection/delivery and the empty mat return can be learned separately; joining requires both, then transfer.

THIRDBIN.title: A third toy destination
THIRDBIN.previousSharedSetup: Three low marked baskets; safe oversized ball, stuffed toy and sturdy supervised rope prop, plus a second suitable example of each if wanted. Skip any toy the dog shreds or swallows.
THIRDBIN.sharedSetupReview: Teach the third toy-destination pairing independently, then combine all familiar examples with positions varied; new examples require teaching.

steps.setup: Put the first two baskets away. Secure the third broad low basket on its own large marker and prepare only its safe familiar toy, with a short clear approach and rewards ready.
steps.decision: The third assignment is independently teachable; mixed choices add the existing two-bin discrimination before more exemplars.

steps.setup: Set all three familiar marked baskets securely with roomy routes, starting close to the third destination. Use only the separately taught safe toys, keep rewards accessible and your pointing hand neutral. Check every toy still suits this dog without shredding or swallowing.
steps.decision: The third assignment is independently teachable; mixed choices add the existing two-bin discrimination before more exemplars.

steps.setup: Prepare one additional safe example at a time with only its matching basket visible. Check each ball, stuffed toy or rope for swallowing and shredding risk; keep other examples out until separately taught.
steps.decision: The third assignment is independently teachable; mixed choices add the existing two-bin discrimination before more exemplars.

PERSON.title: Recognize a familiar person’s name
PERSON.previousSharedSetup: Two familiar willing adults and an enclosed quiet room. No strangers, crowds, restraint or social pressure. Adults use neutral hands and do not beckon during choice trials.
PERSON.sharedSetupReview: Learn each familiar adult name independently, then vary positions and distances so proximity, pointing or the helper calling do not choose the recipient.

steps.setup: In a quiet enclosed room, arrange only the first familiar willing adult nearby. Keep a short clear approach, rewards at that adult and still welcoming hands; no restraint or forced social contact is needed.
steps.decision: Both name-person pairings are independent; equal choices require both before changing relative distance.

steps.setup: Practice with only the second familiar willing adult in the choice area, using a distinct name. Clear a short approach, keep rewards there and put the first adult out of view for this pairing.
steps.decision: Both name-person pairings are independent; equal choices require both before changing relative distance.

steps.setup: Place both familiar adults equally close in a quiet enclosed area. Agree on still hands and no beckoning, prepare rewards at each location and a mixed request order, with room for voluntary approaches.
steps.decision: Both name-person pairings are independent; equal choices require both before changing relative distance.

steps.setup: Keep both familiar adults visible and prepare a small difference in their distances, with clear approaches to each. Agree on neutral hands and no competing food displays, and keep an easy equal-distance reset available.
steps.decision: Both name-person pairings are independent; equal choices require both before changing relative distance.

EQUIP.title: Retrieve your walk kit
EQUIP.previousSharedSetup: A large robust carrier with a safe grasp handle; empty first. A human checks that clips, straps and loops stay protected and removes the leash for fitting. Never mouth metal clips or trail loose equipment.
EQUIP.sharedSetupReview: Retrieve only safe dedicated oversized equipment props; the human alone handles attachment, fit and exit decisions.

steps.setup: Inspect a large robust empty carrier with a safe grasp handle and no loose loops. Keep walking equipment put away, rewards and a receiving hand ready; skip for shredding or unsafe gripping.
steps.decision: A carrier handover uses take/give; station pickup adds retrieve before protected equipment is loaded.

steps.setup: Place the familiar empty carrier at one designated low open station or clear floor spot. Clear a short non-slip return route, with rewards ready and all leads, clips and straps out of reach.
steps.decision: A carrier handover uses take/give; station pickup adds retrieve before protected equipment is loaded.

steps.setup: A human checks that a suitable light walk kit is securely protected inside the familiar carrier, with no trailing straps or mouth-accessible metal. Keep the successful low station and short clear delivery route unchanged.
steps.decision: A carrier handover uses take/give; station pickup adds retrieve before protected equipment is loaded.

TOILETBELL.title: Ring to request a toilet trip
TOILETBELL.previousSharedSetup: A large low-force quiet button at a comfortable nose height near the exit, inaccessible electronics and prompt adult response. A request never replaces regular toilet opportunities.
TOILETBELL.sharedSetupReview: Reward a clear low safe signal and promptly offer an elimination opportunity; the signal is not a guarantee or reason to delay routine outings.

steps.setup: Secure the familiar large quiet low-force button near the usual toilet exit at comfortable nose height, with electronics inaccessible. Prepare an ordinary supervised trip and rewards at the toilet spot; urgent access never depends on pressing.
steps.decision: A familiar pad press is connected to immediate access, then spontaneous requests; toilet needs override training.

steps.setup: At a normal likely toilet time, keep the familiar button reachable and the safe exit route ready for an immediate accompanied trip. Have outdoor equipment accessible and your hands neutral; offer access even without a request.
steps.decision: A familiar pad press is connected to immediate access, then spontaneous requests; toilet needs override training.

steps.setup: Keep the button in its familiar accessible place and arrange prompt adult responses during supervised periods. Have the usual safe route, regular toilet schedule and a simple request log ready; other request signals remain valid.
steps.decision: A familiar pad press is connected to immediate access, then spontaneous requests; toilet needs override training.

LIGHTPAD.title: Turn on a lamp with a pad
LIGHTPAD.previousSharedSetup: A commercially safe accessible low-voltage or wireless control pad, secured wiring and electronics out of reach. Humans configure and inspect the lamp; no plugs, wall switches or electrical DIY by the dog.
LIGHTPAD.sharedSetupReview: Use a large safe disconnected training pad before an adult-controlled action; no mains switch, cord access or unsupervised device use.

steps.setup: Have a human inspect and operate a safe lamp while the room stays otherwise lit. Begin at a comfortable viewing distance with rewards ready; secure wiring and controls away from the dog's mouth.
steps.decision: Lamp-change comfort and disconnected pad pressing run independently; their combination requires both.

steps.setup: Have a human disconnect the lamp from the approved low-voltage or wireless pad. Secure the pad at natural nose height near the familiar target position, with batteries and wires inaccessible and rewards separate.
steps.decision: Lamp-change comfort and disconnected pad pressing run independently; their combination requires both.

steps.setup: After separate light and press comfort, have a human enable the inspected lamp control. Secure electronics out of reach, keep the room otherwise lit and rewards ready, and plan human resets between single presses.
steps.decision: Lamp-change comfort and disconnected pad pressing run independently; their combination requires both.

BLANKET.title: Pull a lap blanket into place
BLANKET.previousSharedSetup: A consenting seated adult, a light loose blanket with a safe broad grip edge and non-slip footing. No cords, knots, trapped limbs or blanket wrapping around the dog; skip for fabric eaters.
BLANKET.sharedSetupReview: Move a light suitable training blanket on the floor without entanglement or swallowing; this does not establish temperature self-management.

steps.setup: Loosely support a lightweight blanket on a low stable chair with a broad safe edge at natural mouth height. Clear all feet and neck from fabric, have a release reward ready, and skip fabric eaters.
steps.decision: The gentle rope-pull component transfers to freely sliding fabric before a tiny lap adjustment and cue.

steps.setup: Seat a consenting adult steadily with the light blanket loose over their knees. Keep a free broad edge away from hands and feet, clear non-slip footing and rewards ready; the adult can help the fabric slide.
steps.decision: The gentle rope-pull component transfers to freely sliding fabric before a tiny lap adjustment and cue.

steps.setup: Use the familiar seated adult and freely sliding light blanket, with the safe edge accessible and no snagged material. Prepare rewards for one small adjustment; the adult will finish positioning and remove fabric after practice.
steps.decision: The gentle rope-pull component transfers to freely sliding fabric before a tiny lap adjustment and cue.

BOXFIND.title: Search a few open boxes
BOXFIND.previousSharedSetup: Wide shallow open boxes without staples or loose pieces, suitable food, and one dog at a time; supervise and skip for paper eaters.
BOXFIND.sharedSetupReview: An obvious accessible reward in one safe open box teaches its own exploration before additional boxes; no unrelated search prerequisite.

steps.setup: Place one broad shallow open box on a clean non-slip floor. Remove staples and loose pieces, separate other animals and prepare a visible suitable reward; choose a plate instead for paper eaters.
steps.decision: An obvious reward in one open box teaches its own search; another food-search lesson adds no necessary component.

steps.setup: Arrange two familiar shallow open boxes with clear walking space around each. Check intact edges, keep other animals separate, and have one suitable reward ready where the dog can watch its placement.
steps.decision: One obvious open-box find teaches its own investigation before adding containers and a tiny hidden choice.

steps.setup: Prepare three familiar safe open boxes in a tiny clear area and a small suitable reward. Keep the dog comfortably nearby during placement and leave every container easy to reach and reveal.
steps.decision: One obvious open-box find teaches its own investigation before adding containers and a tiny hidden choice.

TOWEL.title: Unfold a loose food towel
TOWEL.previousSharedSetup: A clean flat towel, suitable food, and close supervision; skip if fabric is chewed, swallowed, or guarded.
TOWEL.sharedSetupReview: Voluntary comfortable contact with a flat towel precedes wiping; do not cover the face, restrain or assume tolerance of wet grooming.

steps.setup: Lay a clean towel completely flat on a non-slip floor and prepare a few suitable visible food pieces on top. Supervise one dog and skip if fabric is chewed, swallowed or guarded.
steps.decision: Visible food on a safe open towel precedes one loose fold; no unrelated search or retrieve is required.

steps.setup: Keep most of the familiar towel flat and arrange one very loose edge fold over a partly visible reward. Leave a broad open route to the food and be ready to reveal it; no knots or tight rolls.
steps.decision: Visible food on a safe open towel precedes one loose fold; no unrelated search or retrieve is required.

LOSTTOY.title: Find a partly hidden toy
LOSTTOY.previousSharedSetup: A safe favorite toy and an uncluttered room; no high shelves, tight spaces, or forced waits.
LOSTTOY.sharedSetupReview: Visible familiar-toy placement precedes partial concealment and short transfer; no forced wait or unreachable hide is necessary.

steps.setup: Choose the familiar safe favorite toy and a clear floor marker in an uncluttered room. Keep the dog freely nearby, an easy play or delivery reward ready, and all placements at floor level.
steps.decision: A visible accessible favorite toy precedes partial concealment; finding need not include delivery.

steps.setup: Place the familiar toy partly behind a broad stable harmless object, leaving most visible and the access route open. Prepare the familiar play reward and room to reveal the toy promptly; no forced wait is needed.
steps.decision: A visible accessible favorite toy precedes partial concealment; finding need not include delivery.

TRAIL.title: Follow a short food trail
TRAIL.previousSharedSetup: A clean safe surface, suitable food and no other dogs competing; avoid unknown outdoor foods or unsafe ground.
TRAIL.sharedSetupReview: Short safe food trails are enrichment with dog-chosen pace; following visible food is not evidence of operational scent tracking.

steps.setup: Choose clean safe ground with no other animals competing. Prepare a few suitable food pieces about a short paw-step apart, with a clear route beside them and comfortable equipment if needed.
steps.decision: A visible food line precedes one broad bend; it makes no claim to human-scent tracking.

steps.setup: Prepare the same small food trail with one broad easy bend and an accessible finish on checked safe ground. Keep reward spacing close, other dogs away and any lead loose without snag hazards.
steps.decision: A visible food line precedes one broad bend; it makes no claim to human-scent tracking.

HIDESEEK.title: Find a familiar person
HIDESEEK.previousSharedSetup: Two familiar cooperative adults, clear exits and a dog comfortable with brief visual separation; skip for separation distress.
HIDESEEK.sharedSetupReview: Two familiar adults progress from visible to a tiny nearby hide; no prolonged separation or restraint to create excitement.
