steps.setup: Arrange two familiar cooperative adults a few clear steps apart in a quiet space, both visible. Keep rewards at the helper and no restraint; skip if moving away from either person causes distress.
steps.decision: A visible trusted helper precedes partial and tiny complete hiding, with no forced wait or separation test.

steps.setup: Choose a broad open doorway with a clear route and a familiar helper who remains mostly visible behind its edge. Keep the other adult with the dog, rewards at the helper and an immediate reunion available.
steps.decision: A visible trusted helper precedes partial and tiny complete hiding, with no forced wait or separation test.

steps.setup: Use the same open doorway and a familiar helper just behind it, with a short clear route and no closed door. Keep the other adult beside the dog and arrange an immediate gentle voice clue or reunion if needed.
steps.decision: A visible trusted helper precedes partial and tiny complete hiding, with no forced wait or separation test.

NAMEDFIND.title: Find and deliver a named toy
NAMEDFIND.previousSharedSetup: Two safe named toys, easy accessible floor-level placements and a dog comfortable with this small search. No forced waits or separation tests.
NAMEDFIND.sharedSetupReview: Use independent label choices and search components before a broader named-search chain; old partial choices must not credit broader unobserved ability.

steps.setup: Place both familiar named toys fully visible on a clear nearby non-slip floor. Keep your hands and gaze neutral, rewards ready for a familiar give and a mixed label order planned.
steps.decision: Named visible delivery and unnamed hidden delivery run independently; their combination requires both before helper placements.

steps.setup: Put one familiar toy aside and prepare an easy floor-level hiding spot beside a broad stable object. Keep the remaining toy mostly visible, the dog freely nearby and a clear delivery route to your receiving hand.
steps.decision: Named visible delivery and unnamed hidden delivery run independently; their combination requires both before helper placements.

steps.setup: Prepare two easy accessible search spots for the familiar named toys, with at least one toy fully visible initially. Keep routes clear, rewards ready and your cues neutral; avoid tight, high or inaccessible hides.
steps.decision: Named visible delivery and unnamed hidden delivery run independently; their combination requires both before helper placements.

steps.setup: Arrange a familiar helper to change only one easy floor-level placement while you remain neutral beside the dog. Keep new positions visible at first, the receiving hand and rewards ready, and a clear finished cue planned.
steps.decision: Named visible delivery and unnamed hidden delivery run independently; their combination requires both before helper placements.

SCENTMATCH.title: Find one familiar person’s scent
SCENTMATCH.previousSharedSetup: One willing familiar adult, large identical ventilated containers with secured lids, clean cotton samples and clean handling tools. No essential oils, chemicals or ingestible loose samples. One dog at a time; this is a game, not detection certification.
SCENTMATCH.sharedSetupReview: Rename the actual familiar-person odor-versus-blank discrimination; remove the unsupported general reference-matching implication and control handling cues.

steps.setup: Have a willing familiar adult handle clean cotton, then secure it inside a large ventilated container the dog cannot open or mouth. Keep rewards outside the container, with no oils, chemicals or loose samples accessible.
steps.decision: A safe familiar-human sample acquires rewarding investigation before clean comparisons and fresh-sample checks; no oils or operational claims.

steps.setup: Using clean tools, prepare two identical secured vented containers: one familiar-adult cotton sample and one untouched sample. Place them equally near, keep food separate and other dogs away, and avoid differing handling odors.
steps.decision: A nominal blank is not odorless. Match materials and handling and avoid food or helper cues.

steps.setup: Prepare fresh matched cotton samples and identical secured vented containers, with clean tools and a helper. Use the same familiar adult as before, keep food away from samples, balance other handling and plan mixed positions.
steps.decision: One learned target versus a blank is discrimination, not generalized matching-to-sample; remove the misleading reference-sample procedure.

TRACKPERSON.title: Follow a short human trail
TRACKPERSON.previousSharedSetup: Two familiar adults, a safe open low-distraction area, a secured familiar-human cotton scent sample and comfortable equipment if needed. Food stays at the finish, not along the route. No roads, forced separation or real missing-person searches.
TRACKPERSON.sharedSetupReview: Fresh easy route following may use multiple cues; a sniffed sample does not establish matching, and operational identification is not certified.

steps.setup: Choose clear safe ground away from roads and two familiar adults, with one waiting visibly a few metres away. Use comfortable equipment if needed, note the short straight route and keep food only at the finish.
steps.decision: A visible fresh-route introduction precedes an unobserved straight trail using a known scent sample, then one broad bend; visual hide-and-seek and food trails remain separate.

steps.setup: Keep the dog comfortably with you while the familiar helper lays a fresh short straight route to a safe broad screen. Prepare their cotton sample in a secured container at the start, clean equipment and an easily revealed endpoint. Keep the route away from roads.
steps.decision: Offering a sample does not teach its meaning. Route following can use visual, ground-disturbance or airborne cues.

steps.setup: Arrange a fresh five-to-ten-metre route with one broad bend on safe ground while the dog comfortably stays with you. Mark it for the humans, prepare the helper's secured scent sample and an easy finish with rewards, away from roads.
steps.decision: Keep recreational route following distinct from person-specific operational scent tracking.

SCENTINDICATE.title: Show a find with a quiet nose hover
SCENTINDICATE.previousSharedSetup: A large secured vented container with a familiar human cotton scent sample inside. No oils or loose samples. Comfortable natural head height, no prolonged breath holding or sustained nose pressure.
SCENTINDICATE.sharedSetupReview: Shape a brief voluntary nose hover without pawing, pressure or grabbing; an indication is a trained action, not proof of target identification.

steps.setup: Secure the familiar human-cotton scent sample in a large ventilated container at natural head height. Fix it against movement, keep rewards separate and leave room to reset away; no oils or loose samples are accessible.
steps.decision: Gentle investigation is shaped directly into a brief relaxed hover; scent discrimination is independently learnable.

steps.setup: Use the same fixed scent container at comfortable natural head height, with rewards accessible away from it. Keep the dog's head free and turns brief; no nose pressure or prolonged hold is planned.
steps.decision: Gentle investigation is shaped directly into a brief relaxed hover; scent discrimination is independently learnable.

ARTICLE.title: Find a familiar scented article
ARTICLE.previousSharedSetup: A large secured vented container holding clean cotton handled by one familiar adult, safe open hiding places and no accessible samples, oils or food inside. This is recreational searching.
ARTICLE.sharedSetupReview: Finding a familiar container in easy placements can use visual and odor cues; do not label it validated person-scent identification.

steps.setup: Place the familiar secured human-scent container visibly on a clear floor, with food rewards separate in your hand. Keep samples, oils and container contents inaccessible, and leave space to investigate without pickup.
steps.decision: Familiar sample investigation supports visible location before a tiny concealment; retrieving and formal indication remain separate.

steps.setup: Prepare a tiny search area and a broad stable object partly screening the familiar secured container. Leave the access route open and rewards outside it, with the dog comfortably nearby and no climbing or cavities.
steps.decision: Familiar sample investigation supports visible location before a tiny concealment; retrieving and formal indication remain separate.

DIG.title: Dig in a designated patch
DIG.previousSharedSetup: A clean broad shallow digging area with soft suitable material, no sharp pieces or buried food for eaters, and room to leave. Inspect paws and keep dogs separate.
DIG.sharedSetupReview: Use a designated safe accessible digging medium with supervision; no ingestion, competition or inappropriate location testing.

steps.setup: Inspect a clean broad shallow patch of soft suitable material for sharp pieces. Separate other dogs, keep rewards beside the patch and an optional safe toy visible on its surface; leave an open exit and no buried food.
steps.decision: A designated safe patch directly acquires a short optional digging invitation and supported finish.

steps.setup: Prepare the familiar checked digging patch, rewards and a pleasant next activity. Have a safe cover or barrier ready for afterward, keep other dogs separate and supervise for sore paws, grit or swallowing material.
steps.decision: A designated safe patch directly acquires a short optional digging invitation and supported finish.

DRINK.title: Retrieve from a training prop
DRINK.previousSharedSetup: A stable lightweight purpose-built practice cabinet with rounded edges, guarded hinge gaps and no latch or seal. A human controls its easy door travel. Use a non-slip floor and remove the prop and handle after supervised practice. Never use an electrical or food-storage appliance. Use the familiar empty safe carrier on its reachable front shelf.
DRINK.sharedSetupReview: Retire all refrigerator assembly steps without automatic credit; new IDs combine an empty-carrier practice-prop retrieve with optional gentle nudging.

steps.setup: A stable lightweight purpose-built practice cabinet with rounded edges, guarded hinge gaps and no latch or seal. A human controls its easy door travel. Use a non-slip floor and remove the prop and handle after supervised practice. Never use an electrical or food-storage appliance. Use the familiar empty safe carrier on its reachable front shelf.
steps.decision: The new prop chain begins with the learned delivery ending rather than a long novel sequence.

steps.setup: A stable lightweight purpose-built practice cabinet with rounded edges, guarded hinge gaps and no latch or seal. A human controls its easy door travel. Use a non-slip floor and remove the prop and handle after supervised practice. Never use an electrical or food-storage appliance. Use the familiar empty safe carrier on its reachable front shelf. Place rewards ready for both the opening and the delivery.
steps.decision: Joining fluent components does not require withholding a marked reward or increasing pull force.

steps.setup: A stable lightweight purpose-built practice cabinet with rounded edges, guarded hinge gaps and no latch or seal. A human controls its easy door travel. Use a non-slip floor and remove the prop and handle after supervised practice. Never use an electrical or food-storage appliance. Use the familiar empty safe carrier on its reachable front shelf. Decide the ending in advance; dog nudging uses the familiar secure target.
steps.decision: An optional nudge is not a mandatory gate; dog closure still needs its exact component before use.

steps.setup: A stable lightweight purpose-built practice cabinet with rounded edges, guarded hinge gaps and no latch or seal. A human controls its easy door travel. Use a non-slip floor and remove the prop and handle after supervised practice. Never use an electrical or food-storage appliance. Use the familiar empty safe carrier on its reachable front shelf.
steps.decision: A chain cue is introduced after the supported routine, with management and prompt fading kept separate.

SORTALL.title: Sort the toys
SORTALL.previousSharedSetup: Use the individually taught toy-to-basket assignments and three large marked baskets. All objects must suit this dog; reward correct deposits throughout. Do not assume untaught examples will generalize.
SORTALL.sharedSetupReview: Combine individually taught object-destination assignments and new examples gradually; success on six familiar props is not abstract sorting competence.

steps.setup: Secure the three familiar low marked baskets and place one separately taught safe toy for each on a clear non-slip floor. Keep routes equally easy and rewards accessible, with your hands neutral after the invitation.
steps.decision: Known two-bin sorting and third-bin choice precede the whole set; new exemplars are required when introduced, before layout changes.

steps.setup: Keep the marked baskets in their familiar positions and add only one separately taught second example initially. Check every toy for chewing or swallowing risk, clear short routes and prepare rewards for each deposit.
steps.decision: Known two-bin sorting and third-bin choice precede the whole set; new exemplars are required when introduced, before layout changes.

steps.setup: With the dog away, move each familiar basket together with its large marker and shorten the approach routes. Use the same taught safe objects and keep your hands neutral, with rewards ready for deposits.
steps.decision: Known two-bin sorting and third-bin choice precede the whole set; new exemplars are required when introduced, before layout changes.

steps.setup: Prepare a small set of taught safe objects, familiar marked baskets and clear non-slip routes. Have component cues and rewards ready, with a definite end and prop removal after the last deposit.
steps.decision: Known two-bin sorting and third-bin choice precede the whole set; new exemplars are required when introduced, before layout changes.

COURIER.title: Courier to a named person
COURIER.previousSharedSetup: Two familiar willing recipients, safe pouch and tray, flat sender mat and clear indoor routes. Practice only taught names with visible recipients; no delivery of medication, valuables or loose ingestible items.
COURIER.sharedSetupReview: Join recipient discrimination, pouch collection and return only after their components; vary helper positions without pressure or sensitive contents.

steps.setup: Arrange both familiar recipients equally close and still, with an empty safe pouch and a clear route back to the sender's mat. Keep rewards at the ends, hands neutral and no pointing or beckoning planned.
steps.decision: Known person-name discrimination and the reusable delivery round are actual components; recipient choice, collection and cue fading follow.

steps.setup: Keep both familiar recipients visible with clear approaches, changing only a small distance difference. Agree that receiving hands appear after arrival, with no competing food displays or reaching for the pouch, and rewards ready.
steps.decision: Known person-name discrimination and the reusable delivery round are actual components; recipient choice, collection and cue fading follow.

steps.setup: Place the familiar safe pouch with one light protected note on the low tray beside the sender's mat. Keep both named recipients visible and neutral, routes clear and rewards at handover and return; no loose ingestible contents.
steps.decision: Known person-name discrimination and the reusable delivery round are actual components; recipient choice, collection and cue fading follow.

steps.setup: Prepare the familiar low tray, safe pouch, sender mat and short clear routes to both visible willing recipients. Check protected contents and rewards at both ends, with component cues available and a break after one round.
steps.decision: Known person-name discrimination and the reusable delivery round are actual components; recipient choice, collection and cue fading follow.

WALKREADY.title: Ready for a walk
WALKREADY.previousSharedSetup: Secure indoor practice area with a second boundary before any outside exit. Human checks and attaches equipment, holds the lead and controls doors. The dog can leave fitting; no forced sit or unattended leash access.
WALKREADY.sharedSetupReview: Retrieve a dedicated safe prop, voluntarily fit equipment and pause at a secured exit as separate components; humans decide readiness and traffic safety.

steps.setup: In a secure indoor area, prepare the familiar protected walk-kit carrier and comfortable fitting equipment. Have rewards accessible and space for the dog to leave fitting; the human will unpack and remove equipment during rehearsal.
steps.decision: Equipment retrieval and voluntary harness fitting are actual components of this specific project; doorway wait and short loose walking enter only when used.

steps.setup: Prepare the familiar kit and a clear indoor fitting area, with clips and straps accessible to the human. Have rewards ready for the dog's comfortable chosen posture and room to withdraw rather than any restraint.
steps.decision: Equipment retrieval and voluntary harness fitting are actual components of this specific project; doorway wait and short loose walking enter only when used.

steps.setup: Fit and check comfortable equipment, with the adult securely holding the lead. Choose a closed indoor practice door behind a second secure boundary, clear its swing and keep rewards ready for a brief pause.
steps.decision: Equipment retrieval and voluntary harness fitting are actual components of this specific project; doorway wait and short loose walking enter only when used.

steps.setup: Prepare the designated protected kit station, voluntary fitting area and closed practice door with a second boundary. Check the whole indoor route, human access to clips and doors, and rewards for useful pauses; an indoor finish is sufficient.
steps.decision: Equipment retrieval and voluntary harness fitting are actual components of this specific project; doorway wait and short loose walking enter only when used.

RALLY.title: A little rally route
RALLY.previousSharedSetup: A spacious non-slip enclosed area and three clear human-readable stations. No competition precision, tight turns or speed requirement.
RALLY.sharedSetupReview: A short floor-level sequence combines fluent components with generous reward and releases; no competition or orthopedic fitness claim.

steps.setup: Place one clear human-readable station card a few easy steps away in an enclosed non-slip area. Clear the heel approach and stand/release space, with rewards accessible; the dog does not need to read the card.
steps.decision: Short heel and stand form the first station; the independent cone loop is required only when that station joins.

steps.setup: Add a familiar soft cone after the first station with generous walking clearance and a broad loop. Keep the connecting route open and rewards accessible at each finish, with distinct component cues ready.
steps.decision: Short heel and stand form the first station; the independent cone loop is required only when that station joins.

steps.setup: Prepare three familiar stations ending in a comfortable stand and release, linked by broad non-slip walking routes. Keep rewards ready between stations and remove speed, competition precision or tight-turn demands.
steps.decision: Short heel and stand form the first station; the independent cone loop is required only when that station joins.

CIRCUIT.title: A floor-level adventure circuit
CIRCUIT.previousSharedSetup: A wide floor-level hoop, a very short secured open tunnel and ground poles in a spacious non-slip area. All equipment has easy bypasses. No jumps, speed, tight turns or fitness prescription.
CIRCUIT.sharedSetupReview: Combine enjoyable floor-level obstacles with clear exits and comfortable movement; no speed, jumping or physical-conditioning quota.

steps.setup: Secure the familiar wide hoop on the floor and the shortest bright open tunnel far apart on non-slip ground. Clear a straight walking connection and easy bypasses, check snag-free equipment, and have rewards at each exit.
steps.decision: Known voluntary hoop and short tunnel passes link first; ground poles are required only at the step introducing them.

steps.setup: Keep the familiar hoop/tunnel arrangement and add widely spaced secured ground poles beyond it with generous straight clearance. Check ordinary stride spacing and all bypasses, with rewards accessible after each separate piece.
steps.decision: Known voluntary hoop and short tunnel passes link first; ground poles are required only at the step introducing them.

steps.setup: Check the familiar floor-level hoop, short secured open tunnel and widely spaced ground poles in an open non-slip area. Preserve broad connections and bypasses, prepare component cues and rewards, and plan only one easy route.
steps.decision: Known voluntary hoop and short tunnel passes link first; ground poles are required only at the step introducing them.

SCENTREPORT.title: Find, show and report a scent
SCENTREPORT.previousSharedSetup: One secured familiar human-scent container, easy accessible placements and an uncluttered room. No oils, operational searches or prolonged indication.
SCENTREPORT.sharedSetupReview: Find, brief indication and return-touch form a learned recreational chain; this does not validate odor identification or search-and-rescue reporting.

steps.setup: Fix the familiar secured human-scent container in a fully visible nearby floor-level spot. Keep food outside it and accessible beside the find, with room for a soft nose hover and no loose samples or oils.
steps.decision: Visible find-and-indicate chaining needs the visible article approach; partly concealed searching is not yet used.

steps.setup: Use the same visible fixed container and stand only a clear step away. Keep your target hand empty and rewards accessible both beside the find and at your hand, with an unobstructed return route.
steps.decision: Known search and brief indication join first; the separate hand target is required only when adding the report.

steps.setup: Partly screen the familiar secured container behind a broad stable object in the tiny known search area. Keep all access open, stand nearby with an empty target hand, and have rewards and component cues ready.
steps.decision: The partly concealed search component becomes necessary only when this step introduces partial concealment.

ROUTINE.title: A short cooperative trick routine
ROUTINE.previousSharedSetup: An enclosed non-slip space, steady handler and generous curves. Choose only the dog’s comfortable versions; this optional routine requires no speed, music, audience or repeated performance.
ROUTINE.sharedSetupReview: Combine a few comfortable familiar optional movements; short duration and willingness outweigh polish or an imposed performance target.

steps.setup: Choose an enclosed non-slip area with a steady handler and generous space for a natural brief bow and broad circle. Keep rewards accessible and clear room for a full stand reset between actions; no speed or audience is needed.
steps.decision: Known bow and broad circle join with pauses; the independent pose is required only at the final-pose step.

steps.setup: Use the familiar broad circle route and a comfortable pose spot with secure footing. Keep rewards ready and the camera put away, with space for a pause and a clear finished cue afterward.
steps.decision: Known bow and broad circle join with pauses; the independent pose is required only at the final-pose step.

steps.setup: Prepare the familiar comfortable bow, broad circle and brief pose in one open non-slip space. Have individual cues and rewards available between pieces, with an honest break ready after one supported routine.
steps.decision: Known bow and broad circle join with pauses; the independent pose is required only at the final-pose step.
